title: IT Support Manager
description:
Are you ready to get the Easygo Edge?

The IT Support Manager will provide technical, hands-on leadership to the IT Support Officers and act as the escalation for complex IT problems in a fast-paced, global organisation. The role will sit at the intersection of technical delivery, people leadership, and service operations in a newly-created, hands-on technical leadership role.

What you’ll build with us:

You'll be the technical bridge between our IT Support Officers and the Sys Admin team — the person IT Support escalates to when tickets get hard, and the person Sys Admins can confidently hand work down to. You'll own day-to-day service desk operations, but you'll also be expected to roll up your sleeves on complex troubleshooting across endpoint, identity, networking, AV and SaaS.

You'll get to combine deep technical capability with people leadership to drive high-level internal customer service across technology solutions.

We know that innovation ignites when we build and create together, in person. This is a full-time opportunity at our Melbourne office. You’ll work right where it all happens, surrounded by our fearless crew shipping high-impact work.

Who is Easygo?

We’re a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. While they command a fierce global following, our crew is employed directly by Easygo and that’s where the real fun happens.

We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast. People who are ready to Unify, Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact. And that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else.

The impact you’ll make:

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of IT Support Officers, setting clear performance expectations and holding regular 1:1s and team rituals
  • Build a culture of ownership — your team should be proud of what they deliver, not just closing tickets
  • Ensure each team member's yearly individual and developmental goals, along with their 90-day goals, are set, tracked, and adhered to — with regular check-ins to keep progress on course
  • Conduct performance reviews, recognise wins, and manage underperformance constructively
  • Develop onboarding programs and ongoing training pathways so your team is always levelling up
  • Ensure that rosters and coverage models provide adequate support for the business during Australian operating hours.

Technical Leadership & Escalation

  • Act as the senior technical escalation point for the IT Support team — own complex troubleshooting across macOS/Windows endpoints, Google Workspace, identity and access, networking, and SaaS applications
  • Bridge the Support and Sys Admin functions — know when an issue stays at L1/2 and when it warrants L3 engagement
  • Mentor IT Support Officers technically — pair on tricky tickets, run technical deep-dives, and lift the team's diagnostic capability over time
  • Contribute to platform improvements alongside the Sys Admin team — spot recurring tickets that point to deeper systems issues and help drive permanent fixes rather than repeat workarounds
  • Maintain hands-on technical credibility — the team should respect your technical judgement as much as your leadership

Service Desk Operations

  • Own the day-to-day operation of the IT service desk via Jira Service Management — queue health, ticket quality, SLA adherence
  • Triage and prioritise incoming requests and incidents based on urgency and business impact, escalating to Sys Admin as appropriate
  • Be accountable for service desk KPIs: resolution times, first-response rate, backlog, and user satisfaction (CSAT)
  • Produce regular reporting for IT leadership on helpdesk performance, trends, and opportunities for improvement
  • Ensure project work
  • Manage the escalation path clearly — know when to own it, when to delegate and when to escalate

Process & Continuous Improvement

  • Identify and implement process improvements that reduce ticket volume, shorten resolution times, and improve self-service capability
  • Develop and maintain runbooks, knowledge base articles, and SOPs so your team can resolve issues consistently and efficiently
  • Drive adoption of ITIL-aligned practices without the bureaucracy — keep it lightweight and practical
  • Support the transition of IT projects into BAU by building operational processes and training the team before go-live

End User & Office Support

  • Ensure your team delivers excellent support across hardware, software, network connectivity, and SaaS applications for a mixed macOS/Windows fleet
  • Oversee AV and conferencing equipment support across all office locations — meeting rooms need to just work
  • Support joiners, movers, and leavers through IT onboarding and off-boarding processes, working closely with People & Culture
  • Manage IT asset lifecycle — procurement, deployment, tracking, and disposal — with accurate records maintained at all times

Vendor & Stakeholder Management

  • Manage relationships with hardware, software, and service vendors relevant to the service desk function
  • Coordinate with Finance and IT leadership to procure hardware and SaaS tools efficiently and in line with budget
  • Be a visible and credible representative of the IT function in business conversations — you'll deal with stakeholders at all levels
  • Contribute to IT policy development and ensure the team operates in line with Easygo's security and compliance standards

Your track record:

Essential

  • 5+ years' experience in a technical role eg systems administrator or systems engineer
  • 2+ minimum years' experience leading an IT service desk or helpdesk team, including direct people management
  • Strong grasp of service desk operations — SLAs, CSAT, ticket hygiene, queue management, ITIL and KPI reporting
  • Hands-on technical capability across technical support: macOS, Windows, networking basics, SaaS application support
  • Experience with the Atlassian suite - specifically JSM
  • Familiarity with Google Workspace administration and MDM tooling (e.g. FleetDM, InTune)
  • Ability to stay calm under pressure, triage effectively, and lead your team through high-volume periods or incidents
  • Strong communication skills — you can explain the technical to non-technical stakeholders without losing them

Bonus points if you also have:

  • ITIL Foundation certification or equivalent working knowledge of ITIL practices
  • Experience in a high-growth, fast-paced tech or enterprise business
  • Exposure to IT asset management, SaaS lifecycle management, or procurement
  • Comfort with data and reporting — able to pull meaningful insights from ticket data and present them clearly
  • Awareness of compliance frameworks and how they intersect with IT support operations

Here are our benefits and perks:

Sharpening your edge

  • The ultimate sandbox. Exciting, on-the-job learning opportunities.
  • 1-in-3 of our people level up their roles every year. If you deliver, you move.

Competitive pay and bonus scheme

  • Market-synced pay that respects your craft and location.
  • Performance-based bonus recognition based on your impact (up to 20%).
  • Help us build our crew and get paid for it with our high-value referral bonus. Because great people know great people.

Office perks

  • In-house baristas serve you free coffee, fresh juices and smoothies.
  • Daily catered breakfast and regular company-wide events.
  • Snack walls and drink fridges on every floor.
  • Fun, modern office spaces. Pool tables, table tennis, gaming consoles and an F1 simulator.

We play fair. We hire fair.

True to our value of ‘Play fair’ we always hire fair. Our work and our brands are fuelled by our diverse culture. We hire for talent and grit. But we never discriminate. Your race, religion, nationality, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital, veteran, or disability status won’t affect our hiring decision, or your trajectory here. Come as you are and get the Easygo edge.

title: Fleet Performance Manager
description:
We are seeking a proactive and customer-focused Fleet Performance Manager to serve as the primary point of contact for EPC Power’s larger and strategic customers. This role is responsible for ensuring customers have a consistent, reliable interface for account-level communication, escalation management, and operational visibility.


The Fleet Performance Manager must understand system context, terminology, operational states, and common fleet-level issues well enough to engage effectively with internal cross-functional teams. The role also requires translating technical information, analytics, and system status into clear, actionable communication for customer stakeholders with varying levels of technical understanding.


In addition, the Fleet Performance Manager leverages fleet monitoring tools and data analytics to support proactive engagement, early issue awareness, and identification of maintenance or parts opportunities that improve fleet performance and customer satisfaction.

title: IT Specialist (Infrastructure Facilities)
company: Office of the Chief Information Officer
description:
As an IT Specialist (Infrastructure Facilities), you will work across GSA IT organizations providing project management support. Location of position: The Office of Digital Infrastructure Technologies, Infrastructure Facilities Branch. This branch implements, operates, maintains, and supports mission critical systems and applications. Position can be filled in any of the following locations: Washington, DC; Kansas City, MO; Fort Worth, TX; Tacoma WA; Lakewood, CO or Raleigh, NC.

We are currently filling one vacancy, but additional vacancies may be filled as needed. As an IT Specialist (Infrastructure Facilities) you will perform the following duties: Serves as an expert in the Information Technology (IT) field and plays a key role in complex, sensitive, high-level IT work characterized by an exceptional degree of difficulty and responsibility; provides expert technical support, advice, guidance, and assistance to other IT personnel and IT management in the planning and integration of agency-wide and regional network hardware and software in relation to the upgrade and maintenance of new and existing systems and infrastructure. Represents the organization in meetings with representatives of industry, other agencies, public organizations, etc., to resolve problems, develop joint policies and standards and exchanges of information regarding areas of technical expertise; provides project leadership and IT subject matter expertise on GSA IT and customer engagement project teams and fact-finding plans involving multiple large-scale projects, designed to deliver IT and communication services on a nationwide and regional office basis. Provides technical support, advice, guidance, and assistance in planning and integrating agency-wide and regional network hardware and software related to upgrading and maintaining new and existing systems and infrastructure; works with policy officials to develop guidelines and procedures for the agency wide use and management of GSA IT digital and physical infrastructures; determines hardware, software and infrastructure needs and coordinates the deployment of required hardware, software and infrastructure to maintain the integrity and accessibility of systems, platforms, and data centers; monitors infrastructure performance, ensuring optimum performance is maintained at all times. Serves as a senior technical expert on identifying customer needs and requirements; analyzing system requirements; conducting and/or leading lower graded employees in completing IT tasks and projects, cost-benefit analyses, and other research projects; ensuring compliance with laws, regulations, policies, standards and procedures; troubleshoots and resolves complex technical IT issues and determines cost effective viable solutions. Serves as a Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) at a COR FAC II level or higher, monitoring contractor performance and reviewing deliverables; serves on acquisition development and proposal evaluation teams, ensuring procurements are performed accurately, adequately documented, and completed in a timely manner; Identifies appropriate contractual vehicles (schedule contracts, blanket purchase agreements, multiple award contracts, specialized service contracts, etc.) to determine availability and prices of IT goods and services.

If selected, you must meet the following conditions: Current or Former Political Appointees: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C or Non­Career SES employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the HR Office. Failure to disclose this information could result in disciplinary action including removal from Federal Service. Serve a one year probationary period, if required. Undergo and pass a background investigation (Tier 2 investigation level). Have your identity and work status eligibility verified if you are not a GSA employee. We will use the Department of Homeland Security's e-Verify system for this. Any discrepancies must be resolved as a condition of continued employment.

title: SUPERVISORY SECURITY SPECIALIST
description:
You will serve as a SUPERVISORY SECURITY SPECIALIST in the SPECIAL PROGRAMS BRANCH of the FLEET CAPABIITIES and FORCE DEVELOPMENT DIRECTORATE of COMMANDER US FLEET FORCES COMMAND.

You will be responsible for the technical and administrative management of all SAP security functions and SAP security personnel assigned to the command.

You will provide advice on difficult or unusual problems, as well as administrative matters through periodic discussions.

You will make recommendations for appointments, promotions, or reassignments and develop and submit hiring packages as required.

You will direct, manage, and enforce overarching and event-driven security policy and procedures germane to the introduction and implementation of SAPs within USFFC Headquarters and throughout the USFFC AOR.

You will provide a broad range of security functions and highly specialized duties related to the unique operational and administrative requirements of assigned SAPs.

You will strategically leverage limited resources and manpower to ensure continuous application and management of stringent SAP security and compliance controls within administrative and operational environment.

You will establish, review, and/or approve policies and procedures for SAP material and information that satisfy mission requirements of operational commanders and assigned forces while ensuring appropriate security protocols are in place.

You will serve as primary approval authority for all transportation plans supporting the secure movement of USFF SAP material, information, and information systems supporting training, exercises, and operations throughout the USFFC AOR and globally.

You will maintain the DoW/DoN systems of record with current and accurate SAPF accreditation information, to include the documentation supporting SAPF accreditation.

You will direct and supervise investigations into SAP security incidents, determine incident severity, approve corrective actions, direct culpability assessments, and determine security incident characterization.

title: Career Counselor 2
description:
OIC of Washington I Job Description

Position: Career Counselor 2

Division: Education and Career Services

Department: Career Counseling

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities which are required of the employee for this position. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. OIC of Washington is an “at will” employer and employment can be terminated at any time for any reason.


Supervised by: Program Manager

Positions supervised: 0

FLSA classification: Non-Exempt

Minimum Qualifications: BA degree in Social Services or related field. Or four (4) years of experience in a supervisory or leadership role. Or four (4) years of experience in budget development and management. Or additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of education

Job Location: Moses Lake

Salary Range: $23.85 - $31.11 DOE


Position Overview:

The Career Counselor will assist the Manager in achieving programmatic success statewide and target services to migrant seasonal farmworker individuals and/or families. Under the supervision of the Program Manager, this position will work to improve the economic and educational status of eligible students. This position will provide assessments, counseling, education, employment preparation, job development, and related services to adults in a positive and compassionate manner. This position will work with the career counseling services department to provide services to reduce barriers. It is expected that this position will establish strong professional relationships with OIC students, businesses, community partners, and employers to meet program goals and objectives.


Essential Duties:

  • Keep the Program Manager apprised of the progress in meeting monthly and annual goals for the program.
  • Complete the career counseling cohort objectives assigned by the Associate Director and report in a timely manner to the Program Manager.
  • Ensure assessment, counseling, education, employment preparation, and job development services are provided to eligible adults.
  • Manage and guide career counseling cohort in a positive and compassionate manner.
  • Complete an intake interview for potential participants in person and via telephone to determine eligibility for program services.
  • Enroll students and adults who meet eligibility requirements and can provide required documentation into appropriate program services, completing intake forms and getting required documentation.
  • Refer ineligible people to other appropriate service providers, maintaining documentation of the referral.
  • Assess skills, aptitudes, interests, short- and long-term education, training, and career goals, conduct testing, and develop an agreed upon Individual Employment Plan (IEP) for enrolled students and adults.
  • Assess barriers and support service needs of all members of the family unit and make referrals to appropriate providers.
  • Provide emergency services and support services to students.
  • Provide follow up on effectiveness and appropriateness of services provided through referral of students’ family members who are not enrolled in OIC programs.
  • Monitor, review, and document the progress of each participant in meeting the objectives of the IEP. Periodically meet on-site with the program participants and training providers to determine training progress, ensure contract compliance, and resolve any problems.

title: Director, People
description:
Meet Method

Method has built the most modern way to connect to consumer financial accounts. Combining real-time liability connectivity with instant payment execution, Method’s API is designed to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use.

We have helped 45+ million users connect 350+ million liability accounts credential-less and processed over $2.5B in payments, helping users save millions in interest. One in every three credit cards in the United States is in the Method ecosystem and leading financial institutions like SoFi, Bilt, Cleo, Sezzle, Figure & Aven rely on our APIs to build magical experiences for millions of consumers.

We’re a team of 50+ people spread across offices in Austin, SF, New York City, and Washington D.C! We’re excited to continue the momentum working alongside our investors and advisors from Andreessen Horowitz, Emergence Capital, Y Combinator, Avra, and Ardent. To learn more about us, check out our blog!

About the role / The impact

Method has grown to roughly 65 people on a deliberately lean, AI-native operating model, and we are preparing for our next stage of growth. We are hiring our first Director of People to help us build the people strategy that takes us there.

You will be responsible for building and managing all aspects of the HR function, including performance management, compensation and benefits, employee development, compliance, and culture. The ideal candidate has a builder mindset and will have extensive experience in scaling HR teams/programs in dynamic environments.

This is a hands-on role. Some systems are in place; what we need is someone to turn them into programs people trust and processes that scale with us. You will work alongside a strong Talent Acquisition team and a group of sharp generalists across Finance and Operations and oversee one talent and people generalist.

What you'll do

  • Design and lead all facets of the People function at Method

  • Coaching and Development

  • Performance Management

  • Design Method’s total rewards strategy

  • Analytics

  • Operations

  • Reinforce Method's values and culture as we grow.

Who you are

  • 8+ years of progressive HR experience

  • At least 5 years of experience as the primary HR point-of-contact within a high-growth company, preferably in the tech industry

  • You have led or been an early member of the people function at a venture-backed startup, ideally through the Series B to C or D stretch.

  • You came up through people operations, moved into HR business partnership, or vice-versa.

  • You have real employee relations experience and the judgment that comes with it.

  • You are comfortable in a spreadsheet; you can build a compensation or leveling analysis yourself.

  • You have designed performance, compensation, and leveling programs from scratch and adapted them through headcount growth.

  • You build trust quickly and coach leaders with confidence.

  • You bring conviction, and you adjust quickly when something is not working.

  • You prefer building to administering, and you right-size process to the stage of the company.

  • You use AI tools to move faster and think better.

Extra Awesome

  • Experience as the first people hire at a company that scaled past 150.

  • Background in fintech, B2B SaaS, or another high-growth technical environment.

  • Experience running people programs on Rippling.

  • Experience designing equity refresh programs.

  • A creative streak for culture and employee engagement programming.

The annual US base salary range for this role is approximately $180,000 - $215,000 based on experience and location. We also offer an equity package and have a suite of excellent benefits.

Benefits available to full time employees

  • Medical, Dental, Vision; basic medical plans 100% covered

  • Flexible PTO

  • $30/day Lunch allowance when working from the office

  • 12 weeks parental leave

  • Commuter benefits; employer-sponsored

  • Phone/internet stipend

  • WFH stipend

  • Student loan repayment contribution

  • Lifestyle Spending stipend

  • Learning & Development stipend

  • Hybrid-office stocked with snacks

  • Quarterly team off-sites

In-office Policy

For most roles are Method, we expect a regular in-person presence at one of our hubs in NYC, Austin, SF or DC. We have embedded flexibility to work remotely for a week here and there, but the general expectation is a minimum 2-3 days/week in office on average. What does not work is full-time remote.

Accommodations

Method provides reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance with your application due to a disability, please contact us at [email removed] to request an accommodation.

title: Administrative Coordinator, Desert Futures Design Studio
description:

In determining if your employment advances the public interest, the agency will consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Under applicable law, the employment of an individual serving a probationary or trial period automatically terminates when that period ends unless the agency affirmatively certifies, in writing, that the individual's employment should continue and that their appointment should be finalized. We are looking for a hands-on Security Engineer III to strengthen our cloud, application, and infrastructure security. You will work closely with Engineering, DevOps, and IT teams to identify risks, implement security controls, automate security processes, and ensure compliance as we scale.

Key Responsibilities :
• Cloud Security: Secure AWS and GCP environments, including IAM, network security, encryption, logging, and access controls.
• Application Security: Perform security reviews, vulnerability assessments, penetration testing coordination, and remediation tracking.
• DevSecOps: Integrate security scanning into CI/CD pipelines, including SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, container scanning, and IaC scanning.
• Infrastructure Security: Secure Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Linux systems, and cloud infrastructure.
• Security Monitoring: Improve threat detection, security logging, alerting, incident response, and investigation processes.
• Vulnerability Management: Identify, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities across applications, infrastructure, and dependencies.
• Compliance: Support SOC 2, ISO 27001, customer security assessments, audits, and evidence collection.
• Security Automation: Build scripts and tools to automate security checks, reporting, and remediation.
• Incident Response: Investigate security incidents, perform root-cause analysis, and implement preventive measures.
• Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner with Engineering, DevOps, IT, and Product teams to embed security into everyday workflows.

Required Skills :
• 6–10 years of experience in information security, cloud security, application security, or DevSecOps.
• Strong hands-on experience with AWS and/or GCP security.
• Good understanding of IAM, least-privilege access, secrets management, encryption, and network security.
• Experience integrating security tools into CI/CD pipelines.
• Familiarity with tools such as SonarQube, Snyk, Trivy, Checkov, Wiz, or equivalent.
• Working knowledge of Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar technologies.
• Knowledge of OWASP Top 10, common application vulnerabilities, and secure coding practices.
• Experience with vulnerability management, security incident response, and risk assessment.
• Scripting skills in Python, Bash, or similar languages.
• Understanding of SOC 2 or ISO 27001 requirements.

title: Principal CPI Analyst IV
location: Albany, GA — on-site at the Government facility
description:
This is the analytical center of the contract and the hardest billet to fill. The Principal CPI Analyst IV owns the Enterprise CSM Metrics Scorecard — building it, validating it, and briefing it monthly to the Marine Corps SECREP Working Integrated Product Team — and leads Lean Six Sigma process improvement across the Marine Corps secondary reparable supply chain. The work is genuinely technical: extracting data from a dozen Government systems, running statistical models to forecast supply chain trends, mapping value streams, and writing the courses of action and POA&Ms that change how the Marine Corps manages reparables.


Key Responsibilities

• Use Lean Six Sigma methodologies to drive Continuous Process Improvement across the CSM program.

• Facilitate the SECREP Working Integrated Product Team (WIPT); brief the Enterprise CSM Metrics Scorecard and supporting analysis; capture business and action items in meeting minutes and the CSM POA&M.

• Develop, maintain, update, validate, and archive the Enterprise CSM Metrics Scorecard presentation (due monthly, before the third Thursday).

Build and maintain tools that extract data from Marine Corps systems to give visibility of key performance metrics.

• Collect metrics data, perform calculations, develop statistical summaries, and perform trend analysis across the supply chain — 21 defined metrics including maintenance failure rate, SECREP ‘R’ rating, excess over Economic Retention Quantity, backorder customer wait time, fill rate, MRP credits, IMA washout and repair rates, and Invalid SECREP Exchanges.

• Use statistical tools — design of experiments, hypothesis testing, correlation, regression — to test hypotheses and forecast trends.

• Conduct root-cause investigations and value stream mapping to develop Courses of Action and Plans of Action and Milestones.

• Develop, refine, standardize, and execute processes that ensure metrics data integrity.

• Collaborate with the Government to refine metrics and set target ranges.

• Develop responses to internal and external SECREP data calls; provide input into policy changes and facilitate them.

• Conduct RIP site visits in support of CPI initiatives; analyze RIP Situation Reports and maintain stakeholder communication throughout process evaluation.

• Provide project and change management support to the Government customer.

title: Facilities Project Manager
description:
Every successful building project needs someone who speaks both languages: construction and operations.


Camelot Facility Management is hiring a Facilities Project Manager to represent the facilities team onsite with our client on a multi-year expansion project in Boston’s Back Bay, from design review and shutdown coordination through punch lists, commissioning, and turnover. You’ll bring operational realities into project meetings, coordinate the logistics that keep work moving safely, and make sure every finished space and building system is ready for live operations.


This is a facilities-side project role with no budget or contract authority. The project management team owns cost, contracts, and change orders. You own the facilities perspective: making sure operational requirements, logistics, and turnover are handled right. If your career blends facilities management and project management, and you’re the person people go to for a clear answer, this role was built for you.


Responsibilities

  • Be the connector. Serve as the primary liaison between the design and construction team and the client’s facilities leadership. Represent facilities requirements in project meetings, report status and emerging risks to stakeholders, and escalate issues that can’t be resolved at the working level.
  • Build operations into the plan. Partner with project management on project schedules, risk mitigation, and contingency planning so operational requirements are built in from the start.
  • Keep the building running. Coordinate contractor site access, loading docks, and staging with construction and security. Coordinate planned shutdowns, utility outages, and systems testing to minimize disruption to occupants and operations.
  • Catch it early. Conduct first-pass reviews of MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) and building systems designs. Coordinate full technical reviews with the client’s facilities team and send comments back to engineering.
  • Close it out right. Serve as the client’s primary point of contact for punch lists and project closeout as each construction phase finishes and track every item to resolution.
  • Keep people informed. Coordinate with the client’s internal communications team on occupant-facing announcements about project activity.
  • Hand it over ready. Collect and organize turnover documentation, including O&M manuals, record drawings, warranties, and commissioning reports, and enter it into facility management systems (CMMS) as needed, so facilities staff can support new systems from day one.

title: Senior CX Insights Manager, APAC
description:
About Crunchyroll

Founded by fans, Crunchyroll delivers the art and culture of anime to a passionate community. We super-serve over 100 million anime and manga fans across 200+ countries and territories, and help them connect with the stories and characters they crave. Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.

Join our team, and help us shape the future of anime!

About the Role

Crunchyroll is seeking a Senior Manager, CX Insights (APAC) to lead our Customer Experience (CX) Insights function across APAC. Reporting to the Director of CX Insights & Analytics, this leader will transform customer feedback, operational data, and market insights into actionable recommendations that improve the fan experience and influence business strategy.

This is a highly visible role that sits at the intersection of Customer Experience, Analytics, Product, Content, Marketing, Subscription, and Customer Support. You will be responsible for developing a comprehensive understanding of the APAC customer journey, identifying opportunities to improve satisfaction and loyalty, and championing the voice of the customer throughout the organization.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical expertise, customer obsession, business acumen, and a deep understanding of the APAC market. They are equally comfortable diving into data, presenting executive-level insights, and leading high-performing teams.

What You'll Do

Lead Customer Insights Strategy

  • Own the CX Insights strategy for the APAC region, ensuring alignment with Crunchyroll's global customer experience objectives.
  • Build a holistic view of the customer journey by integrating feedback, behavioral, operational, and market data.
  • Develop frameworks to measure customer sentiment, loyalty, satisfaction, effort, and retention drivers across the region.
  • Identify emerging customer trends, pain points, and opportunities that influence strategic priorities.

Drive Actionable Business Impact

  • Translate complex data into compelling narratives and recommendations that influence decision-making across Product, Marketing, Content, Subscription, Commerce, and Customer Support teams.
  • Establish scalable mechanisms for surfacing customer insights to stakeholders and leadership.
  • Partner with regional and global teams to prioritize initiatives that improve customer satisfaction and business outcomes.
  • Quantify the impact of customer experience improvements and track progress against key performance indicators.

Lead Voice of the Customer Programs

  • Own and evolve Voice of the Customer (VoC) programs across APAC.
  • Design and optimize customer listening strategies, including surveys, feedback programs, support interactions, social insights, and community feedback.
  • Ensure customer feedback is systematically captured, analyzed, and integrated into business planning.

Build World-Class Analytics & Reporting

  • Develop executive-level dashboards, reporting frameworks, and performance reviews.
  • Leverage advanced analytical techniques to identify drivers of customer behavior and sentiment.
  • Partner closely with Analytics, Data Science, and Research teams to enhance measurement capabilities and predictive insights.
  • Champion data quality, governance, and best practices for customer insights.

Lead and Develop Talent

  • Build, mentor, and inspire a high-performing team of insights professionals.
  • Foster a culture of curiosity, accountability, innovation, and customer obsession.
  • Establish clear goals, development plans, and career growth opportunities for team members.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience in Customer Experience, Customer Insights, Consumer Research, Analytics, Business Intelligence, Strategy, or related fields.
  • Including 3+ years of people leadership experience managing high-performing teams.
  • Proven experience leading customer insights programs within a subscription, digital product, streaming, entertainment, technology, or consumer-focused business.
  • AI and technology-forward mindset with experience evaluating and adopting innovative tools and methodologies to improve the speed, scale, and quality of customer insight generation.
  • Strong analytical capabilities with experience working across large datasets and customer feedback ecosystems.
  • Expertise in Voice of the Customer methodologies, customer satisfaction measurement, and customer journey analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and drive cross-functional alignment.
  • Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive presentation skills.
  • Professional fluency in English.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working across multiple APAC markets.
  • Familiarity with streaming, media, entertainment, gaming, or fan-driven consumer businesses.
  • Experience with customer feedback platforms, survey tools, CRM systems, and modern BI solutions.
  • Knowledge of advanced analytics, predictive modeling, experimentation, or customer segmentation methodologies.

Success in Your First Year

In your first year, you will:

  • Establish yourself as the leading voice of the APAC customer within Crunchyroll.
  • Build trusted partnerships with regional and global stakeholders.
  • Elevate the maturity of our Voice of the Customer and CX measurement programs.
  • Deliver insights that directly influence customer experience improvements and business performance.
  • Develop a scalable framework for understanding and communicating the evolving needs of anime fans across Asia-Pacific.

Why you will love working at Crunchyroll

In addition to getting to work with fun, passionate and inspired colleagues, you will also enjoy the following benefits and perks:

  • Best-in class medical, dental, and vision private insurance healthcare coverage
  • Access to counseling & mental health sessions 24/7 through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Free premium access to Crunchyroll
  • Professional Development
  • Company's Paid Parental Leave
  • up to 26 weeks for birthing parents
  • up to 12 weeks for non-birthing parents
  • Hybrid Work Schedule
  • Paid Time Off
  • Flex Time Off
  • 5 Yasumi Days
  • Half-Day Fridays during the summer
  • Winter Break

title: SECURITY SPECIALIST (TRAINING SPECIALIST)
description:
This National Guard position is for a SECURITY SPECIALIST (TRAINING SPECIALIST), Position Description Number D2161000 and is part of the Oregon National Guard 173rd Fighter Wing, National Guard.

As a SECURITY SPECIALIST (TRAINING SPECIALIST), GS-0080-9, this position is located in an Air National Guard Wing (ANG), Mission Support Group, Security Forces (SF) Squadron. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the subject matter expert in managing the SF Squadron program to include Air Expeditionary Force (AEF) deployments, formal training programs, and readiness and emergency management. Provides guidance and recommendations to the squadron commander on all aspects of SF programs for military personnel management, budget and management analysis, training, and training resources for drill-status personnel. 1. Reviews all operations, mobility, contingency, and exercise plans to ensure combat readiness for the SF Squadron. Analyzes exercise and contingency plans to determine required SF actions in support of mission requirements. Evaluates all equipment, manning and training requirements to meet wartime, contingency, deployment, and pre-planned tasking. Coordinates with other base organizations on applicable plans. Manages the development of plans for deployment, disaster preparedness, base recovery, contingency response, and other related plans. Prepares, updates, and reviews the SF portion of the base deployment, disaster preparedness, base recovery, contingency response, and related plans. Coordinates plans and annexes with SF supervisors. Initiates changes, modifications, additions and deletions to personnel and equipment tasking and assignments through the SF Commander for approval. Iidentifies deficiencies develops, and implements plans for increasing mission readiness. Ensures the SF unit meets requirements for wartime capability and AEF requirements. 2. Responsible for proper security, classification, and storage of classified documents. Compiles information by identifying shortfalls and recommending corrective actions to Status of Resources and Training System (SORT) monitor on the status of SF personnel and training in all three classified reports. Serves as the alternate SORTs monitor. 3. Oversees the coordination, review, and implementation of SF manning authorizations and military personnel assignments. Creates and implements the unit Force Management Plan for all Unit Type Code (UTC) teams as directed by MAJCOM. Recommends organizational change and identifies needs or problem areas. Initiates operational and administrative actions in support of unit manning authorizations and coordinates with base training, recruiting, and ANG NGB/A7S. Reviews Force Package and UTC posturing. Monitors personnel who are affected by Air Force (AF) Specialty conversion actions and makes team assignments. Implements change to the mobility requirements and resource roster. Monitors personnel readiness. Implements AOR Reporting Instructions and local directives for the establishment and management of AF Deployment Folders. 4. Serves as the SF commander's key staff member responsible for the overall management of the unit-training program by overseeing the planning, organizing, directing, operating, and evaluating all unit training related items. Must make instant decisions and select a course of action under high stress conditions. Serves as a training consultant to all unit members and determines if quality-training programs are in effect within all sections. Communicates effectively, orally and in writing, to prepare and present briefings, coordinates planning efforts and manages program activities. Implements and manages training programs, policies, and procedures, as directed by higher headquarters, commanders, and Base Training. Develops, manages, and conducts training in support of garrison and expeditionary mission requirements. Advises and assists commander and unit personnel in executing their training responsibilities. Prepares a budget to support training requirements and submits to unit commander. Develops and coordinates training policy and program changes (including publications, supplements, and operating instructions) with work centers, unit commander, and other training managers, as appropriate. Advises the unit commander and supervisors of personnel skill level progression. identifies training actions required to maintain unit combat readiness. Prepares and briefs the monthly Status of Training report to the Unit Commander. Coordinates and schedules personnel to attend USAF technical schools and other formal training. Coordinates civilian training seminars, workshops, etc. Verifies eligibility of personnel requesting schools. Identifies, analyzes, forecasts, and submits formal school quotas and workday requirements. Serves as squadron program manager for Professional Military Education. 4. Performs other duties as assigned. *The above description only mentions a limited amount of the position's official duties. For a full comprehensive document that covers all the duties of the position, please contact one of the Recruitment Specialists at the bottom of the announcement.

title: Statistician
description:
This position is based at the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System within Medical Research Service. The mission is to develop and test innovative care models and health systems interventions which markedly improve the effectiveness and value of VA health care, while advancing scientific methods for accelerating multi-level adoption, implementation, spread and sustainability of practice-based evidence.

The major duties of the Statistician include, but are not limited to: Participates in a research study and ensures that the research design is properly followed. Prepares the research instruments to collect quantitative data. Selects subjects according to criteria for inclusion and obtaining informed consents. Collects data and ensures that instruments are consistently and properly administered. Ensures reliability and validity of the data. Responsible for the adequacy of methods selected and the accuracy of the results obtained. Conducts and records interviews with subjects as required by the research design. Categorizes and analyzes qualitative data obtained from interviews; Determines which facts may be validly expressed quantitatively. Carries out project proposal with extreme precision. Recognizes variations in statistical findings which demand prompt action in connection with adjusting or changing procedures. Develops and modifies methods used in research studies. Compiles data from existing Medical Center records; abstracts existing documents and categorizes quantitative/qualitative data obtained from documents. Develops and implements data management activities; organizes data entry, produces and edits computer datasets, applies appropriate statistical techniques and performs statistical calculations in analysis and description of the data and interpretation of results. Adapts established statistical methods to specific problems. Writes reports and presents findings in the most pertinent form such as tables, overheads and slides. Drafts a proposal for a subsequent study based on the baseline data and a thorough review of the professional literature. Reviews the quality of data to assure that the data collection instrument is being consistently and properly administered by testing for interviewer reliability and for problems or variations in the data. Participates in meetings with the principal investigator (PI) and the research assistants to develop the details of public health studies. Develops data management details, organizes data entry, produce and edit computer datasets, develop and update data screening programs in appropriate programming languages. Selects appropriate statistical techniques and perform complex statistical calculations in preliminary, intermediate and final analysis, in description of the data and in interpretation of results. Recommends types of further analysis to be done. Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00 am - 4:30 pm Telework: Not available. Virtual: This is not a virtual position. title: Senior People Consultant EMEA
description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

The Team

At Okta, the Manager Success team helps managers lead effective teams through an AI-first support model that combines digital coaching and self-service resources with experienced human advisory. AI-powered guidance serves as the first point of support for everyday leadership and people-management questions, while People Consultants provide individualised coaching and problem-solving when situations require deeper diagnosis, judgment, or expertise beyond standard resources. The team partners with AI resource teams, Enablement, and regional specialists to strengthen manager capabilities and continuously improve the support experience.

Role

The Senior People Consultant leads the team's most complex and ambiguous advisory cases across EMEA, providing advanced coaching and trusted counsel on sensitive leadership, performance, and organisational challenges. Applying deep consulting expertise and sound judgment, this role navigates competing perspectives, entrenched behavioural issues, and complex team dynamics where standard approaches are insufficient.

Beyond individual case ownership, you will elevate the team's effectiveness through peer coaching, complex case reviews, reusable guidance frameworks, and insights that improve AI-enabled support and address recurring organisational challenges. You will also partner with Employee Relations & Compliance (ER&C), Employment Legal, PBPs, Labor Relations, works councils, and regional specialists as appropriate.

Responsibilities

  • Provide advanced coaching to managers and senior leaders on leadership effectiveness, employee development, team dynamics, organisational change, and complex performance challenges.
  • Lead the assessment and resolution of highly ambiguous or sensitive cases by diagnosing root causes, evaluating competing perspectives, and advising on decisions that balance business priorities, employee experience, and organisational risk.
  • Guide leaders through entrenched resistance, difficult conversations, and high-impact decisions while reinforcing accountability for outcomes and sustainable solutions.
  • Exercise advanced judgment within established decision rights, identifying risks and ensuring sensitive, high-impact, or jurisdictionally complex matters follow appropriate escalation pathways to ER&C, Employment Legal, PBPs, Labor Relations, works councils, or regional specialists.
  • Strengthen team capability through peer coaching, complex case reviews, and reusable frameworks that improve diagnostic skills, case strategy, and escalation judgment.
  • Analyse recurring case patterns and AI-supported interactions to identify gaps in guidance and opportunities to improve AI resources, workflows, knowledge content, and decision guardrails in partnership with Enablement and technology teams.

Requirements

  • Deep professional expertise and practical consulting experience across Human Resources, HR Business Partnering, Employee Relations, management consulting, leadership coaching, or organisational development, with a strong focus on navigating complex performance management and remediation.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead and resolve highly complex, ambiguous advisory cases requiring advanced judgment, structured problem-solving, and cross-functional coordination.
  • Proven experience advising senior leaders on sensitive leadership, performance, team effectiveness, and organisational challenges.
  • Exceptional coaching, communication, influencing, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to challenge assumptions, navigate competing perspectives, and guide leaders through difficult decisions.
  • Strong understanding of leadership effectiveness, organisational dynamics, performance management, conflict resolution, risk assessment, and appropriate escalation practices.
  • Familiarity with EMEA employment practices and employee representation processes, including works councils, is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop colleagues through peer coaching, case consultation, knowledge sharing, or reusable advisory frameworks.
  • Experience evaluating or improving AI-enabled workflows, automated guidance, knowledge resources, or digital service capabilities to enhance manager support.
  • Additional language skills are a plus, particularly Spanish, German, or French.

title: Ammunition Inspector

location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit .

About the role

We are looking for a Director of Government Affairs to join our growing Government Affairs & Strategy team. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Government Affairs & Strategy, you will serve as one of CHAOS's principal strategists on defense appropriations, acquisition policy, and program funding. You will build and execute a legislative strategy aligned to our core technologies, represent CHAOS before Congress and the Executive branch, and partner with the Growth team to win new programs and protect existing ones.   • Build bipartisan relationships with Members, committee staff, and personal offices, and extend that network into OSW, the services, and relevant agencies
  • Track the annual NDAA and appropriations cycles from budget request through markup and conference, translating developments into clear guidance for program and executive teams
  • Draft legislative and report language, appropriations requests, and policy briefs
  • Represent CHAOS on Capitol Hill and in industry associations and coalitions
  • Ensure compliance with lobbying and disclosure laws and support PAC and political engagement strategy

We're looking for someone who has:

  • A university degree and 12+ years of relevant experience, or an advanced degree and 10+ years
  • Extensive Congressional experience on defense authorization or appropriations bills
  • Deep knowledge of the NDAA and annual appropriations processes
  • Established bipartisan relationships with relevant Congressional offices and committees
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A results-oriented, self-starter mindset that thrives in a fast-paced, rapidly growing environment
  • Willingness to register as a lobbyist

Nice to have:

  • Experience as a defense appropriations staffer or professional staff member on a defense Committee
  • An active security clearance
  • Prior experience in a corporate government affairs office or as a registered lobbyist
  • Knowledge of the planning, programming, budgeting, and execution (PPBE) process
  • Technical fluency in autonomy, sensing, or AI
  • A willingness to treat no task as too small
  • Sense of humor


Why CHAOS?

  • Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company
  • Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more
  • Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code
  • Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses
  • Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

description:

We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

Meet the Secret Media Team

Secret Media Network is a digital media group focused on recommending perfect plans, discovering great places, sharing things to do and relevant breaking news in different cities around the world. Our family is composed of Valencia Secreta, Barcelona Secreta, Secret LA, Secret NYC, Secret London, Paris Secret, Madrid Secreto, and more!

  • Creating social media posts, writing video captions, liaising with our marketing team to ensure we’re optimising copy to drive sales and/or awareness, or covering a branded event using Instagram stories.

  • Generate creative ideas for new campaigns, and manage final feedback from our clients to ensure everything is on point.

That said, this position sits firmly within the editorial team, and you will be expected to have a solid understanding of the Secret Media Network’s native storytelling tone.

We're seeking someone who:
  • Has 3-5 years of relevant editorial experience.
  • Native-level proficiency in written and spoken French is essential. A fluent English for internal communications is also preferred.
  • Some demonstrable previous digital writing experience (either editorial or commercial).

  • A flair for all things social media, including a sharp sense of what makes a story engaging.
  • The ability to remain calm and organized under pressure, managing a multitude of to-do's across different projects at any one time.
  • An up-to-date understanding of the industry and how native marketing works.
  • Creative and commercial insight, with brilliant storytelling skills.
  • A knack for coming up with excellent ways to connect different brands with our audience.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
Today's most tomorrow company.

We built the world's most powerful battery, the 850MW Waratah Super Battery, and now we want a Senior Project Manager to help us build even more BESS Assets.

We're leading the energy transition towards a better, brighter tomorrow. The work you will do makes a real and very tangible impact on the future of the planet and its people. We're 200 people around the world with 40 GWh of projects moving through development across Australia, Japan, the US and Germany.

Akaysha build, own, and operate our assets. We don't hand a project to someone else once it's approved. The people who design a battery site are the same people who help build it, optimise it and solve the challenges that come with operating it every day.

In this hybrid role, reporting to the General Manager, Delivery, you’ll be accountable for the end-to-end delivery of Akaysha Energy’s utility-scale battery energy storage projects. You will provide leadership across complex contractual, technical, and stakeholder interfaces.

What you'll do

  • Take the lead on utility-scale BESS projects from development through construction, commissioning and handover
  • Bring teams, contractors and partners together to keep projects moving safely and successfully
  • Own budgets, schedule, risk and delivery performance
  • Work closely with EPC contractors, OEMs, network providers and stakeholders to navigate challenges and unlock solutions
  • Lead and support your project team, creating clarity, momentum and shared accountability

How you'll make a positive impact

  • Bring proven experience delivering large-scale energy or infrastructure projects
  • Use your BESS, grid and EPC knowledge to make confident, practical decisions
  • Spot risks early and find solutions that balance technical, commercial and delivery outcomes
  • Build strong relationships across technical, commercial, regulatory and community stakeholders
  • Bring calm, collaborative leadership to complex projects and help your team achieve their goals

Why you’ll love working here

  • Flexibility first: we're hybrid by design, averaging 60/40 office and home split, and real trust to flex that mix when life calls for it.
  • Room to look after yourself: $1,500 a year for your wellbeing, plus $2,000 and two extra days off for your own development.
  • Genuinely generous parental leave: because family isn’t something you fit around a job
  • A stake in what we build: on top of your salary and twice-yearly bonus, permanent team members also share in the value we create through our Long Term Incentive Plan.

Lead the energy transition with us. Apply now.

We believe diverse teams build better solutions for the planet and its people. We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and able to do their best work, no matter their background, identity, or lived experience.

title: Program Analyst (Acquisitions)
company: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
description:
The Program Analyst position is in the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, Department of the Chief Information Officer, Policy and Resources Management Division (PRMD), Vendor Management Branch (VMB). PRMD manages and oversees the administrative functions of the judiciary's national information technology program. VMB provides program offices with analytical, consulting, and document review support for IT hardware, software and services acquisitions.

The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, Department of the Chief Information Officer, Policy and Resources Management Division (PRMD), Vendor Management Branch (VMB) seeks a Program Analyst (Acquisitions). PRMD manages and oversees the administrative functions of the judiciary's national information technology program. VMB provides program offices with analytical, consulting, and document review support for IT hardware, software and services acquisitions. This Program Analyst (Acquisitions) serves as a Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) and provides consultation on contract management and acquisition strategies to IT program managers and technical and financial specialists. These activities involve market research, development and review of acquisitions documents, and evaluation of cost and pricing strategies. The Program Analyst (Acquisitions) reviews solicitations to ensure requirements, goals, and objectives correctly represent the needs of the program office. The incumbent serves on source selection panels and works with program office stakeholders to resolve acquisition-related problems impeding IT project and program goals and objectives. This position will heavily focus on software license agreements. This position reports to the Chief of the Vendor Management Branch. The duties of the position include, but are not limited to: Serving as a COR in pre-award functions, including developing contract requirements, such as statements of work, market research, independent government cost estimates, and evaluating performance criteria for IT hardware, software, and services acquisitions. Serving as a subject matter expert on contract vehicles and potential methods of procurement. Serving as a COR for IT hardware, software, cloud services, IT Security services and IT services contracts, and as technical liaison between the Contracting Officer and the contractor. Maintaining COR files. Providing expert procurement advice to the IT program office and working groups. Serving on technical evaluation panels. Developing functional and technical requirements for enterprise scale hardware and software acquisitions in coordination with AO offices and technical advisory and working groups. Participating in post-award orientation conferences. Monitoring and recording contractor performance or delivery issues and ensuring contractors properly corrects defects. Advising the Contracting Officer of performance issues and the need to issue change orders or contract modifications. Reviewing and processing contractor Invoices. Conducting contract closeouts.

title: Financial Assistance Advisor
description:
Overview

Financial Assistance Advisor

This position will work at ECPI University’s Charlotte, NC campus location.

Transform your Career at ECPI University

Since 1966, the dedicated employees at ECPI University have helped students achieve their goals via practical training and career-focused education with over 50 Associates, Bachelor’s and Master’s Programs. Our culture is to prioritize our students’ success through the support of our dynamic team and industry focused curriculum.

Visit www.ecpi.edu/employment to learn more about how you can help people improve their lives through education.

Position Summary

Are you seeking a financial advising career at a university that promotes the enhancement of each student’s professional and personal life through education? Then a career as a Financial Assistance Advisor with ECPI University may be for you!!

The Financial Assistance Advisor is responsible for providing financial aid support and advising services to both incoming and existing students. This position oversees the daily processing flow and communicates updates to assigned students working through the Financial Aid Office. Advisors must possess critical-thinking skills and use a variety of communication methods and analytical skills to guide and encourage students through the financial aid process. Advisors must build and foster strong relationships with students to support their educational goals.

Responsibilities

  • Advises students about methods to pay for their education, financial aid eligibility, application procedures, financial assistance programs, costs, indebtedness, money management and financial planning; individualizes information to the needs and situation of the student.
  • Collects and/or analyzes financial data on students to determine financial aid eligibility and makes awards within federal, donor and/or institutional guidelines.
  • Evaluates unusual/mitigating circumstance documentation or information provided by the student; exercises judgment by making adjustments or revisions to costs, contribution, need or dependency status as exceptions to the prescribed process.
  • Answers questions, inquiries or requests from students, parents, or guardians in person or in writing regarding financial aid programs and eligibility.
  • Analyzes system generated reports such as grades and enrollment status or award status to verify continued compliance and eligibility of students receiving aid under federal and institutional guidelines; notify students of changes in eligibility of awards and alternatives to amend the situation.
  • Interfaces with students and lenders, employers and/or Student Services staff to resolve concerns.

Qualifications

Education/Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred.
  • 2-3 years of related experience.
  • Any equivalent combination of education, experience, and/or training.

Skills/Abilities

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
  • Proficiency in CampusVue Student database, preferred.
  • Utilizing AI tools preferred.
  • Well-developed oral and written communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational and analytical skills.
  • Ability to quickly master new methodologies, technologies, and systems.
  • Ability to handle a high-pressure environment with significant timeline pressures.
  • Able to interact with employees, potential students, and outside contacts of all levels, providing excellent customer service.
  • Ability to work independently and with a team as well as with various constituents.

Benefits of Employment

ECPI University provides a comprehensive benefits program designed to help our faculty and staff stay healthy, feel supported, and maintain a work/life balance. To learn more about benefits at ECPI University, click HERE.

Committed to excellence and innovation, ECPI University is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

title: Senior Business Analytics Manager
description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

As a Senior Business Analytics Manager, you'll use data to strengthen Compliance across three priorities: Trusted Data, Growth Enablement, and Proactive Risk Prevention. You'll help ensure that regulatory reports, audit responses, and legal evidence are reliable, traceable, and reusable, while transforming customer, transaction, and financial data into actionable insights.
You'll partner with Compliance, Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Business teams to build trusted data foundations, automate recurring requests, and create metrics that reveal operational effectiveness and compliance friction. You'll also conduct root cause and control-gap analysis, help remove compliance-related business roadblocks, support market and licensing initiatives, and surface risks before they are identified externally.
What You'll Be Doing:
  • Facilitate and govern internal and external data requests across OKX global entities, ensuring timely, first-time-right delivery for regulatory reporting, audits and exams, and legal evidence.
  • Build and maintain request records, evidence and definition libraries, and data-governance records to improve data reliability, traceability, and reusability.
  • Productize high-frequency recurring requests into automated or self-service data pipelines, improving turnaround time and cost efficiency.
  • Build and automate Compliance dashboards based on North Star metrics as well as input and guardrail metrics to provide transparency into operational effectiveness, customer and platform risk, and business friction.
  • Conduct deep-dive, root-cause, and control-bypass analyses to proactively identify and prevent compliance risks.
  • Partner with Compliance, Business, Marketing, and local market teams to remove compliance-related roadblocks in current operations and support new markets, licences, applications, and market-access assessments.
  • Collaborate across Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Finance to continuously improve data pipelines and analytics products.
What We Look For In You:
  • Relevant working experience of at least 7 years. (must)
  • Proficiency in database management systems like MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, or PostgreSQL. (must)
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. (must)
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail. (must)
  • Hands-on experience with machine learning algorithms and AI tools. (nice to have)
  • Strong compliance domain knowledge, including KYC, AML, the Travel Rule, insider trading controls, and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions. (nice to have)
  • Experience supporting regulatory reporting, regulatory examinations, and internal or external audits. (nice to have)
  • Preferred industries are Fintech, Digital Payment, Tech companies. (nice to have)
Perks & Benefits
  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • Wellness and meal allowances
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependents

title: Senior Product Designer (AI Builder)
description:
Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution.

Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.

From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech

Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.

Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.

Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.

We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.

But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors, you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.

About the Role

This role exists because we believe the future of design is fundamentally agentic. You're not here to use AI as a productivity tool - you're here to redesign the entire practice of design itself. Part engineer, part designer, part systems architect, entirely at the frontier.

Roles & Responsibilities

  • Set the new standard : Be the living proof of AI-native design workflows. Build remarkable things, show them to the team.
  • Build the stack : Ship projects that progressively automate the design process - from discrete tools to full end-to-end automation.
  • Enable the org : Build AI workflows that 60 designers can run end-to-end - independently, without bottlenecks. Raise the floor.
  • Find the friction : Research where designers get stuck. Turn those observations into tools, agents, and systems.
  • Stay ahead : Maintain frontier knowledge of AI possibilities. Not as a hobby - as a core job function

You are an Ideal fit, if you are

  • Top percentile in AI × Design : You apply AI to product design workflows better than almost anyone. You've proven it.
  • Credible designer and builder : You have taste and you ship. Both matter equally here.
  • Exceptional communicator : Whether 1:1 or to a group - you make complex ideas land simply.
  • Systems thinker : You solve entire classes of problems, not individual tasks.
  • Obsessively curious : Dissatisfied with what exists. Energised by what's next.

What You Get :

  • Virtually unlimited AI compute budget.
  • Work with 60 talented designers who are eager to transform.
  • Direct access to Design, Product, and Company leadership -zero bureaucracy.
  • Full independence to build and experiment.
  • Authority to drive adoption - if it's worth doing, it will happen.
  • The most interesting AI-design infrastructure problem in global tech.
Razorpay believes in and follows an equal employment opportunity policy that doesn't discriminate on gender, religion, sexual orientation, colour, nationality, age, etc. We welcome interests and applications from all groups and communities across the globe.

Title: Student Re-Engagement Specialist

Reports to: Director of Programs

FSLA Status: Exempt - Full-time

Salary Range: $47,000.00/yearly

-

Job Summary

The Student Re-Engagement Specialist (SRS) provides support to re-engage students with their education, whether virtual, hybrid, or in-person. The SRS is responsible for identifying barriers that impede student learning and attendance, addressing issues related to these barriers, providing support, and mentoring students to promote increased attendance, improved academic performance, and social-emotional success.

-

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Identifies students who are disengaged from learning and/or school, particularly those who meet the established definitions of unlawful absences
  • Provides support to students in accessing technology (devices, connectivity, software) that is essential to virtual learning
  • Performs outreach to disengaged, truant, or transient students and their parents/caregivers to provide assistance with re-engaging with school
  • Tracks data and interventions in CISDM
  • Meets with students and families to develop attendance improvement plans; monitor student progress towards meeting plan goals
  • Participate in home visits in collaboration with district attendance officer as needed
  • Make referrals to internal and external resources as appropriate
  • Attend truancy proceedings with district representative as appropriate
  • Monitor and evaluate service to maximize effectiveness and impact quarterly
  • Coordinate program reporting for the school site, and accurately report data to CISPA state office, the designated school district, and other partners or funders.
  • Serve as an ambassador of CISPA through regular communication with school district personnel, students, families, volunteers, and community partners.
  • Participate actively as a member of the CISPA team
  • Other duties as assigned

-

Position Structure

This is a year-round, full-time, non-exempt position with renewal based on annual funding. It is also a benefits eligible position.

-

Benefits Include:

  • Eleven Company-Paid Holiday Periods
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Plans
  • Voluntary Lines of Coverage
  • 401K Contribution
  • Dependent Care FSA
  • Parental Leave

-

Reasonable Accommodation

Communities in Schools of Pennsylvania, Inc. will make reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job
