title: Peer Specialist
description:
This Peer Specialist position may only be filled with a Veteran that meets statutory requirements that are detailed in the qualifications section.

Restricted to VETERANS - See Requirements and Qualifications for details. Special authorities include: Former overseas employees and foreign service employees. Clarification for these authorities is provided in the questionnaire. First AOC (Area of Consideration) is Facility employees; Second AOC is VA Agency; Third AOC are all other eligible applicants. Restricted to VETERANS - See IMPORTANT NOTICE. Open to current, permanent employees of the VA (i.e. T38, T38 Hybrid, and VCS employees on excepted appts covered by an interchange agreement); Federal employees on a Career/Career-Conditional appt.; Former competitive civil service employees eligible for reinstatement; Veterans eligible under VEOA, VRA, and 30% DAV; Those eligible under the Employment Program for People with Disabilities; and those eligible for CTAP/ICTAP. The Peer Specialist functions as an interdisciplinary team member, assisting physicians and other professional/non-professional personnel in a rehabilitation treatment program. Peer specialists perform a variety of therapeutic and supportive tasks that include assisting Veterans in articulating their goals for recovery and personal wellness, learning, and practicing new skills, helping them monitor their progress, assisting them in their treatment, modeling effective coping techniques and self-help strategies based on the peer specialist's own recovery experience, and supporting them in advocating for themselves to obtain effective services. This position will serve as a community-based peer specialist within the local VA facility catchment area. The working environment may include providing peer support services in places such as Veterans' homes, prisons, jails, treatment courts, shelters, tent encampments, street outreach, etc. Duties include, but not limited to the following: Participates in the service, training, consultation, and other professional activities of VA health care services and functions as a fully vested member of the multidisciplinary team. Uses personal recovery experiences to model coping techniques and recovery tolls to coach Veterans to relevant skills need for self-management of their health condition(s) and pursuit of their personal wellness. Observes behaviors that might indicate difficulty adapting or responding to treatment (e.g., missed assessment appointments, failure to attend or maintain abstinence, risk to self or others, disruptive behavior), completes appropriate documentation, and reports concerns to the treatment team in a timely manner. Uses ongoing individual and group meetings to teach Veterans how to identify and combat negative self-talk and overcome fears by providing a forum that allows Veteran to share their experiences. As necessary, handles crisis interventions for Veterans and addresses other emergent situations without the benefit of specific instructions. Informs Veterans about VA and community supports and resources, including how to effectively utilize them in the recovery and wellness process. Maintains a working knowledge of current trends and developments in holistic approaches in wellness and recovery by reading books, journals, and other relevant materials. Accompanies Veterans to appointments as needed, whether medical, housing, or other treatment plan goal appointments, either through agency vehicle or public transportation. Assists Veterans to identify resources and problem solve how to overcome barriers so that the Veterans can independently address transportation and other personal needs. Subsequent background checks may be required if treating Veterans in an institutional setting Performs other related duties as assigned. Work Schedule: Monday - Friday 8:00 am - 4:30 pm (PST) Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Position Description/PD#: Peer Specialist/PD99327S, PD99326S, PD99325S, and PD99324S Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Critical Skills Incentive (CSI): Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not authorized Promotion Potential: This position involves a multi-grade career ladder. The selectee may be promoted to the full performance level without further competition when all regulatory, qualification, and performance requirements are met. Selection at a lower grade level does not guarantee promotion to the full performance level.

You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job. You must have a full, current, and unrestricted peer specialist certification to meet this qualification requirement for employment in VHA as a peer specialist. You must be a Veteran - See IMPORTANT NOTICE. You must have a valid, state-issued driver's license, have a safe driving record, and demonstrate that you are medically qualified to operate the appropriate motor vehicle safely. To be considered for this position, you must complete all required steps in the process. In addition to the application and questionnaire, this position requires an online assessment. The online assessment measures critical general competencies required to perform the job. Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959. Subject to background/security investigation. Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued dentification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment. Participation in the seasonal influenza vaccination program is a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP). As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period or 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

title: Client Relations Representative - Chesapeake, VA
description:
POSITION: Client Relations Representative

Location: Chesapeake, VA

Schedule: M-F 8:30am - 5pm + Local Travel

FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt


Who We Are

At Retirement Income Source, a Sound Income Group company, we empower clients through education-driven financial planning. Our seven-step process helps avoid common retirement pitfalls while aligning strategies with long-term goals. We believe peace of mind comes from understanding your options and making informed decisions with a trusted advisor.


We foster a collaborative, performance-driven culture rooted in integrity, innovation, and service. If you’re enthusiastic about making a measurable impact in the financial services space, we invite you to grow with us.


Position Summary

This is a sales-focused client relationship and business development role, not a traditional administrative support position.


The Client Relations Representative (CRR) serves as the first point of contact for prospective and existing clients while driving appointment generation, supporting advisor growth initiatives, and creating an exceptional client experience. This role is responsible for converting warm leads into qualified appointments, executing marketing events, supporting new client onboarding, and maintaining consistent outreach activity that contributes directly to advisor production and firm growth.


Success in this role is measured through appointment generation, client engagement, event execution, outreach activity, and overall contribution to advisor and business growth.


Key Responsibilities

Sales Development & Appointment Setting

Approximately 70% of this role is phone-based client outreach and relationship-building activity.

  • Conduct outbound follow-up with workshop attendees, seminar leads, marketing inquiries, referrals, and existing clients.
  • Generate and schedule qualified appointments for Advisors.
  • Re-engage inactive prospects, dormant leads, and appointment no-shows.
  • Maintain consistent follow-up cadences until prospects are booked, declined, or disqualified.
  • Build rapport and establish trust through professional, consultative conversations.
  • Accurately document all client interactions and activity within CRM systems.
  • Track and report key performance metrics, including outreach volume, appointments scheduled, kept appointments, and conversion outcomes.
  • Collaborate with Advisors to identify opportunities for increased client engagement and business development.

Marketing & Event Execution

In partnership with Advisors and the Marketing team:

  • Support the planning and execution of workshops, seminars, client appreciation events, and community outreach initiatives.
  • Coordinate event logistics, including venue communication, RSVPs, attendee tracking, room setup, and marketing collateral.
  • Assist with attendee registration, check-in, and event-day support.
  • Conduct same-day or next-day follow-up with attendees and no-shows to maximize appointment conversion opportunities.
  • Represent the firm professionally at public-facing events and engage with prospective clients.
  • Provide event feedback, attendance reporting, and recommendations for improving event effectiveness and return on investment.

Operational Excellence

  • Maintain accurate client records and CRM data integrity.
  • Monitor and report on outreach activity and performance metrics to support business objectives.
  • Partner with Advisors and internal teams to ensure seamless client experiences.
  • Demonstrate accountability for individual performance goals and team success.

title: Management and Program Analyst
description:
Incumbent serves as the Management and Program Analyst, Financial Analyst, for the Resource Support Team, AJV-E630.

Provides a wide range of administrative and analytical duties in the conduct of projects and studies of substantive functions to improve the overall work operations of the organization assigned. Assignments cover one or more of the following functional areas: program planning, execution and control (i.e., program/system planning and evaluation, program performance measurement); management improvement and control (i.e., quality management, organizational planning and development, staffing utilization, productivity, work improvement and work methods, work measurement and staffing standards development, delegation of authority, goals and objectives, and records and information management); and business management. Serves as a subject matter expert (SME) who specializes in the development of new and innovative approaches, methodologies, techniques, and process improvement, e.g., business acumen. Supports evaluating the relationships between major program changes and status of organizations through partnership with analysts and SMEs to create actionable products that provide predictive and prescriptive analytics to enable informed management decisions. Develops procedures, systems, and methods on a variety of management functions and activities in one or more of the following areas - organizational planning and development, staffing utilization, productivity, work improvement and work methods, work measurement and staffing standards development, delegation of authority, goals and objectives, business management, financial tracking and/or information management. Plans, schedules and conducts analyses/studies of proposed program plans for accomplishing program activities. Leads or personally performs complex or controversial studies which result in authoritative recommendations to improve organizational structures, management policies, and work distribution. Leads or personally completes analyses of critical programs by developing baseline performance measurements and comparing performance with the baseline. Prepares long-range (5 year) and short-range planning guidance in accordance with broad agency program policies and objectives. Develops resource (staffing and funding) guidance for subordinate activities, and performs continuous appraisal of the utilization of command resources in accomplishing program objectives and goals. Develops staffing and manpower standards covering complex program functions or missions involved in supply chain management, training, research, information management etc. Projects typically involve development of new approaches to identifying meaningful workload factors and performance quality levels, and determining accurate measurement techniques. Reviews and analyzes new and proposed regulations to determine impact on program operations and management. Responsibilities may involve providing advice and support to management personnel for best utilization and reprogramming of resources, conducting cost versus benefits analyses, developing/maintaining financial tracking systems, monitoring expenditures and developing quarterly/annual/interim reports as required.

title: Case Manager Supportive Housing
description:
Case Manager - Supportive Housing



Make a Difference. Build Connections. Support Recovery.


At Wyandot Behavioral Health Network (Wyandot BHN), we believe everyone deserves the opportunity to live a healthier, more fulfilling life. Our team is passionate about helping individuals overcome challenges, build on their strengths, and achieve greater independence.

We're looking for a compassionate, motivated Case Manager to join our community-based team serving adults living with severe and persistent mental illness. This is an opportunity to do meaningful work every day by building trusting relationships, connecting people with essential resources, and helping individuals navigate life's challenges.

If you're passionate about helping others, enjoy building relationships, and want a career where your work has a lasting impact, we'd love to have you join our team.


What You'll Do

As a Case Manager, you'll be a trusted advocate and partner in each individual's recovery journey. You'll help clients identify their goals, overcome barriers, and access the services and support they need to thrive.

  • Build meaningful relationships with individuals and families through compassionate, respectful, recovery-focused support.
  • Empower individuals to reach their goals by conducting strengths-based assessments and developing personalized service plans.
  • Coordinate care and services with behavioral health providers, medical professionals, hospitals, families, and community partners.
  • Connect clients with resources for housing, healthcare, employment, transportation, financial assistance, and other essential needs.
  • Advocate for individuals when working with healthcare providers, courts, government agencies, and community organizations.
  • Support clients through challenges and crises by coordinating appropriate services and helping them navigate difficult situations.
  • Monitor progress and celebrate growth by evaluating individual needs and adjusting service plans to support continued recovery.
  • Maintain accurate documentation that meets agency, Medicaid, and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate and continue learning through team meetings, clinical supervision, training, and professional development.
  • Work in the community by meeting clients where they are and, when appropriate, providing transportation to appointments and services.

What Makes You Successful

You'll thrive in this role if you're someone who values relationships, approaches challenges with patience and empathy, and believes in helping others recognize their potential.

Success in this position includes:

  • Providing person-centered services that promote recovery, stability, and independence.
  • Helping clients navigate complex systems and access the right resources.
  • Building positive relationships with clients, families, and community partners.
  • Balancing client needs with timely documentation and productivity expectations.
  • Working independently while contributing to a supportive, collaborative team.
  • Demonstrating professionalism, cultural awareness, sound judgment, and respect for every individual.

title: Budget Analyst
description:

Serve as the lead budget analyst in the Business Resources Division, Great Lakes and Ohio River Division (LRD).

title: Food & Beverage Team Leader - Doha Education City
description:

Requirements

  • Proactive and excellent organizational skills.

Experience

If this sounds like you and you are ready to work in an environment that values your work and rewards you fairly, then please click on the "I'm interested" button and join the team!

title: Senior Product Designer - Private Dining
description:
About OpenTable:

With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

The opportunity:

You’ll be joining the growing Private Dining Team in Australia and help elevate OpenTable’s newest line of business. The team is building the next generation event management for our top restaurant groups. We're deeply involved from concept, prototyping, implementation, delivery, to customer validation. We believe in empowering individuals to do phenomenal work.

As a Senior Product Designer on Private Dining, you’ll get to:

  • Lead initiatives that give restaurateurs new and meaningful ways to efficiently manage their private dining operations
  • Have direct impact on consumer facing experiences for our private dining offerings in the OpenTable app
  • Become an expert in restaurant operator workflows by facilitating research with restaurant owners and staff.
  • Use systems thinking to scale solutions across our platform.
  • Work closely with a smart and collaborative team of product designers, product managers, and engineers to deliver experiences that help restaurants provide the best hospitality for their guests.

How we design for restaurants

Your skills and experience:

You enjoy solving complex design challenges and have strong visual and interaction design skills. You have an exceptional portfolio that showcases a breadth of product design work. You also have:

  • Strong at designing and solving for complex or B2B2C workflows.
  • The ability to negotiate, prioritize, and break down design work into measurable outcomes.
  • Strong systems thinking and able to design for multiple platforms (web and mobile).
  • High level of confidence and pragmatism about the design direction.
  • Strong at leading and facilitating workshops with cross-functional partners.
  • Strong product and business thinking.
  • Great written and verbal communication skills.
  • Led user interviews and testing of designs.
  • Experience working closely with product and engineering in an agile environment.
  • At least 5 years of product design experience.\
  • Fluency in AI tools such as Cursor, Figma Make or Claude.
  • Expertise in Figma and other prototyping tools.

If you think you are qualified for this role but don’t tick every box, please apply for the role. The perfect candidate doesn’t exist.

When applying, please include a resume (including a password to your portfolio) and a PDF or link to an online portfolio. Here’s our guide for how to nail design portfolios and presentations.

Benefits and Perks:

  • Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
  • Focus on mental health and well-being:
    • Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
    • Company-paid subscription to Headspace
    • Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)
  • Paid parental leave
  • Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday
  • Paid volunteer time
  • Focus on your career growth:
    • Development Dollars
    • Leadership development
    • Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings
  • Travel Discounts
  • Employee Resource Groups
  • Annual health and wellness reimbursement
  • Monthly social events
  • Free lunch 2 days per week

Work Environment & Flexibility

At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.

Inclusion

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.

If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, or on the job, we’re here to support you. Please reach out to your recruiter to request any accommodations.

title: Environmental Protection Specialist
description:

title: Product Owner, Technology
description:
Guild Mortgage Company, closing loans and opening doors since 1960. As a mortgage banking firm, we are dedicated to serving the homeowner/buyer. Our goal is to provide affordable home financing for our customers, utilizing the best terms available while providing a level of professionalism and service unsurpassed in the lending industry.

Position Summary

The Artificial Intelligence Technology Product Owner is responsible for managing the development and delivery of various Artificial Intelligence products and services supporting IT and Business partner initiatives. The Artificial Intelligence Technology Product Owner works closely with the product team, which consists of AI Analysts, AI Engineers, Data Scientists, Data Architects, Front End Developers, and other cross-functional teams (both internally to IT as well as the business), to define the product vision, a business and technology roadmap, features, and user stories. The Technology Product Owner also oversees the product backlog, which is a list of tasks and requirements for the product, and prioritizes the tasks according to the business value and customer feedback. The technology product owner ensures the product meets quality standards, aligns with business goals, and delivers value to customers and stakeholders within executive resource and budget limits.

Compensation

This role is an exempt position with a Targeted Salary Range of $120,000 to $150,000 annually.

Compensation at Guild is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to local and federal minimum wage requirements, education, level of experience, and applicant’s geographical location.

Essential Functions

  • Define and validate the product requirements, features/epics, and user stories and ensure that they are clear, concise, and testable.
  • Oversee and prioritize the product backlog to ensure alignment with the product vision and roadmap, while accurately representing customer requirements and expectations.
  • Work with the members of the product team and business owners to plan and execute the product development sprints and releases and provide them with the necessary guidance and support.
  • Review and accept the product deliverables and provide feedback and guidance to the development team and ensure that they meet the acceptance criteria and quality standards.
  • Manage the product lifecycle and ensure that the product meets the quality standards, compliance requirements, and business objectives, and delivers value to the customers and stakeholders.
  • Responsible for the successful execution of the current sprint and prepping for the upcoming sprint.
  • Accountable for consistently delivering product sprint goals.
  • Establish velocity of the team to provide insights on forecasting future efforts.
  • Work with BA/Dev/QA Leads and others to ensure all disciplines are acting cohesively to meet sprint goals.
  • Manages sprint priorities in accordance with product roadmap.
  • Proactively engage with business stakeholders to support new feature rollouts.
  • Break down work in consumable parts to ensure regular demos are conducted with key stakeholders.
  • Ability to identify future dependencies and plan for those dependencies.
  • Manage sprint planning, reviews, and retros.
  • Responsible for actively communicating to key stakeholders when sprint goals are in jeopardy.
  • Proactively take steps to remove blockers.
  • Create facts-based, metrics-driven project dashboards for all technology workstreams to provide visibility on progress week over week.
  • Partner with EPMO reporting team to improve how we use JIRA as our source of truth.
  • Perform other duties, as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelors or Master's Degree in computer science, business, logistics or related field to the position, preferred.
  • A combination of education and experience may be considered in lieu of the Bachelor’s degree.
  • Minimum five years' experience as a product owner, product manager, business analyst, or similar role in a digital product development environment.
  • PMI, PMP, PMI ACP; or CSM certification or equivalent preferred. ITIL knowledge preferred.
  • Experience supporting enterprise reporting, business intelligence, analytics platforms or data-focused technology teams.
  • Strong knowledge of agile methodologies, tools, and best practices, such as Scrum, Kanban, Jira, Trello, etc.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and leadership skills, and ability to work effectively with multiple stakeholders and manage conflicting expectations and priorities.
  • Ability to think strategically, creatively, and analytically, and to translate customer needs and expectations into product requirements, features, and user stories.
  • Ability to deliver high-quality products that meet the customer needs, expectations and provide value to the customers and stakeholders.
  • Solid understanding of software development life cycle models as well as expert knowledge of Agile and traditional Waterfall project management principles and practices.
  • Extensive experience working with vendors and offshore resources.
  • Proficient level of technical background to provide leadership to development teams and to be able to accurately and objectively evaluate complex product risks and issues.
  • Experience with Release Management and ensuring the business is fully engaged when releasing new features.
  • Proactive in ensuring the business is aware of upcoming deployments and features.
  • Strong Jira knowledge preferred.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills required.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented; ability to work in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment required.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, Word, Excel, Wiki, collaborative cloud-based programs, and third-party software applications required.
  • Commitment to company values.
  • Customer Service - Proactive attention to each person
  • Integrity - Do and say what's right
  • Respect - Treat others with dignity
  • Collaboration - Listen and work together
  • Learning - Seek knowledge and strive for improvement
  • Excellence – Deliver the unexpected

Supervision

  • Job Scope: Plays a key role in area by generating insights and ideas on policies, processes, procedures, and efficiency; contributes ideas to strategic and operational plans to ensure alignment

  • Complexity: Problems are often complex and specialized and may involve unprecedented circumstances; resolution requires investigation, analysis and review of professional/organizational standards

  • Impact: Decisions and actions have an impact on the smooth operation and timeframes of the department, programs/projects; impact on the broader organization is generally indirect

  • Interaction/Supervision: Acts as a mentor/guide to less experienced professional contributor staff in a similar role; works independently and only under general direction; guided by professional standards, desired outcomes, and project plan specifications

  • Number of Indirect Reports: 10-15

Requirements

Physical: Work is primarily sedentary; mobility in an office setting.

Manual Dexterity: Ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboards

Audio/Visual: Ability to accurately interpret sounds and associated meanings at a volume consistent with interpersonal conversation. Regularly required to accurately perceive, distinguish and interpret information received visually and through audio, e.g., words, numbers and other data broadcasted aloud/viewed on a screen, as well as print and other media.

Environmental: Office environment – moderate noise, no substantial exposure to adverse environmental conditions.

Mental: Learn new tasks, remember processes, maintain focus, complete tasks independently, and make timely decisions in the context of a workflow. This role requires effective adaptation to workplace stressors, including customer service complaints, security responsibilities, and competing priorities. Must be able to adhere to process protocol. Must be able to apply established protocols in a timely manner.

Schedules: Work is primarily performed during the business week, Monday - Friday

Guild offers a pleasant work environment, competitive compensation and excellent benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, LTD and 401(k) with employer match.

Guild Mortgage Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Electronics Engineer
description:
This position is part of the WAPA-RMR-Rocky Mountain Region or WAPA-UGPR-Upper Great Plains Region. As Electronics Engineer, you will provide engineering expertise to develop, upgrade, and operate the Region's communication systems, SCADA systems, operations support systems, telemetering equipment, data distribution systems, and remote telemetry units (RTUs).

As an Electronics Engineer, you will: Applies or adapts automated processes that modify real-time control systems and automated computing systems to solve inherent problems or enhance performance of existing systems. Establishes system design technical requirements, defines engineering approaches to be used in the system design as well as constraints and standards to be applied during the design process. Develops and maintains guidelines, requirements, instructions and procedures relating to the power communications system. Makes analysis of equipment failures and system malfunctions and recommends and/or initiates adjustments, repair, replacement, or other appropriate action to prevent recurrence. Provides communications and system control engineering assistance and advice to the field offices. Monitors maintenance programs to assure necessary actions are implemented on a consistent basis throughout the Region. Provides technical advice and guidance in the resolution of engineering problems arising in ongoing automated systems.

Must be a U.S. Citizen or National. This employer participates in the e-Verify program. Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for Selective Service. Suitable for Federal employment, as determined by a background investigation. May be required to successfully complete a probationary/trial period. Employees serving on a probationary or trial period may be terminated at any time during the probationary or trial period for performance, conduct, or business-related reasons in the interest of Federal service. Security clearance and associated requirements- Moderate Risk. Shift work and emergency overtime may be required. Employee may be required to work other than normal duty hours, to include evenings, weekends and/or holidays. Total salary varies depending on location of position.

title: Manager Orion Program
description:
Serves as Manager of the Orion Program, responsible for managing all the elements of the Orion Program for the purpose of facilitating the development of a human capable vehicle to support the U.S.A. human exploration capability design framework beyond low Earth orbit reference missions. This position reports to the Artemis Program Manager and has critical interfaces with Agency and Center leadership.

The Manager Orion Program: Provides program management and control; program integration and risk management; effective cost control; and requirements and configuration development and control. It is also responsible for execution of the Orion Program's budget, schedule, and technical management. Establishes and implements Orion policy, directs and controls schedules, plans, and execution of the Orion Program design, development, test, production, and operations. Provides the Program management function for Orion prime contractors and Agency Partners. Manages integration across spacecraft subsystems and engineering cross-cutting functions and supports the up and out systems integration efforts of the Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD). Oversees development and implementation of sustaining engineering processes, ensuring critical skill retention and management and operation of the real-time engineering support to the on-orbit vehicle. Manages design and development of required ground operations, flight operations, and ground operations procedures, processes, and facilities in support of vehicle developmental and operational testing. Ensures flight/ground safety while meeting system performance requirements and achieving mission objectives. Implements designs for the Orion spacecraft and ground systems to achieve efficient and effective operations. Oversees associated mission operations and launch and entry suit requirements. Implements systems and tools required for program control including resource and contract management, cost and risk assessment, schedule oversight and management, configuration management, and program documentation. Represents the Orion Program to external entities related to Orion development and acquisition and coordinates requirements with senior NASA officials, other Government agencies, and the private and international sectors. Facilitates a positive working relationship between NASA field centers and Program contractors to ensure that timely decisions are made and communicated across all functional disciplines. This close teaming approach requires positive and extensive NASA/contractor interaction throughout the Program and at all levels.

title: PROGRAM ANALYST (DATA AND ANALYTICS)
description:
You will serve as a PROGRAM ANALYST (DATA AND ANALYTICS) in the FLEET DATA ANALYTICS OFFICE of COMMANDER US FLEET FORCES COMMAND.

You will lead the development of data and analytics solutions to support readiness outcomes in support of the Fleet Data Analytics Office.

You will create value through data exploitation; envisioning development and implementation of data-enabled strategies; enabling business outcomes through analytics and aiding in enterprise information policy.

You will ensure analytic projects are designed to deliver improved readiness outcomes by demonstrating clear alignment to business value drivers.

You will work with business partners to understand business priorities, identify strategic initiatives, and develop effective and timely analytic solutions.

title: GENERAL ENGINEER
description:

You will serve as the principal Technical Warrant Holder for SE and ALRE systems engineering across the Naval Aviation Enterprise (NAE).

You will serve as the expert in SE/ALRE systems engineering life-cycle policy, and provide authoritative advice that shapes major acquisition Programs, sustainment strategies, and future capabilities.

You will identify and resolve real fleet issues related to complex and complicated SE and ALRE.

You will provide expertise in all areas of the acquisition lifecycle (ideation, development, prototyping, testing, production, fielding, and in-service) of a broad range of programs across both SE and ALRE.

title: Lead, AI Governance
description:
Guild Mortgage Company, closing loans and opening doors since 1960. As a mortgage banking firm we are dedicated to serving the home owner/buyer. Our goal is to provide affordable home financing for our customers, utilizing the best terms available while providing a level of professionalism and service unsurpassed in the lending industry.

Position Summary

The AI Governance Lead plays a critical role in the organization by leading the company’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance program. The role is responsible, under general direction, for leading and continuously enhancing the frameworks, policies, and controls that ensure AI and LLM tools and technologies are adopted responsibly, securely, and in compliance with applicable regulations. This role works as part of the IT Governance Team and serves as the primary liaison across Information Security, Software Engineering, IT Operations, Risk, Legal and Compliance to identify, assess, and monitor AI-related risks. Key focus of the position is leading the AI Tool Inventory, Assessment, and Approval Process, AI due diligence and ongoing monitoring activities, and the continuous enhancement of the company’s AI governance strategy, policies, and controls in support of compliance with applicable regulatory requirements as they relate to Information Technology, Security, and Artificial Intelligence.

Compensation

This role is an exempt position with a Targeted Salary Range of $109,114.00 to $156,510.56 annually.

Compensation at Guild is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to local and federal minimum wage requirements, education, level of experience, and applicant’s geographical location.

Essential Functions

  • Serve as the subject matter expert and primary point of contact for AI/LLM governance across the organization, partnering with Information Security, Software Engineering, IT Operations, Risk, and Legal/Compliance to ensure responsible use of artificial intelligence.
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously enhance the company’s AI Governance Strategy, framework, and supporting policies in alignment with industry standards such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Own and maintain the AI Tool Inventory, Assessment, and Approval Process, ensuring all AI/LLM tools, models, and use cases are identified, evaluated for risk, and approved prior to deployment.
  • Lead AI Due Diligence and Ongoing Monitoring activities for third-party and internally developed AI/LLM solutions, coordinating with Third Party IT Risk, Information Security, and Software Engineering stakeholders.
  • Coordinate the Copilot / ChatGPT / Claude Citizen Development Process, establishing guardrails and approval workflows for business-led development of AI-powered solutions.
  • Lead governance of AI agentic tools (e.g., Claude Cowork and similar platforms), ensuring appropriate controls, access management, and change management practices are followed.
  • Develop and maintain the AI Record Retention Policy in partnership with IT Governance, Data Privacy, and Legal/Compliance to ensure AI-generated content and interactions are retained and disposed of appropriately.
  • Own the ongoing enhancement of the company’s AI Use Policy, incorporating emerging risks, regulatory changes, and lessons learned from operational incidents.
  • Partner with Information Security on LLM monitoring and control activities (e.g., SOC monitoring of Copilot/ChatGPT/Claude usage), AI Connected App approvals, AI data loss prevention (DLP) controls, and AI data exposure monitoring.
  • Document and monitor AI governance activities, ensuring tasks, decisions, and control activities are tracked and operate in a well-managed environment.
  • Produce governance deliverables, including AI risk assessments, process flows, procedure documentation, and specialized reports related to AI tools, controls, metrics, and communications.
  • Maintain AI risk management policies, document control gaps and issues, and coordinate efforts to build awareness and understanding of AI governance concepts across business lines.
  • Support implementation of AI governance practices and procedures by preparing and delivering presentations and training to internal stakeholders, providing regular updates on new requirements and controls.
  • Participate in high-level discussions to identify and respond to AI-related business risks, ensuring business units understand key AI risk concepts and their relevance to core business practice.
  • Monitor that controls used to mitigate AI-related business risks are properly designed, executed, and documented; work with cross-functional resources to identify, design, and test controls for optimal effectiveness.
  • Monitor that appropriate management ownership exists to facilitate due diligence and participation in AI-related compliance, audit, and risk management requirements.
  • Support audits and regulatory examinations related to AI/LLM usage, monitoring the disposition and resolution of related issues and findings.
  • Track emerging AI regulations, industry standards, and best practices (e.g., U.S. state AI laws, NIST, ISO/IEC 42001) to ensure the company’s AI governance program remains current and defensible.
  • Promote a culture of continuous improvement and responsible AI use, establishing visible metrics and KPIs to measure the effectiveness of the AI governance program.
  • Collaborate in the development of company-wide governance frameworks encompassing ITIL, CobIT, and ISO disciplines as they apply to AI/LLM technologies.
  • Look for continuous improvement and cost-saving opportunities related to AI tooling and governance processes. Make recommendations to the Director of IT Governance for changes that would result in improved delivery of services and/or cost savings.
  • Participate in strategic and tactical initiatives involving AI-related resource management, monitoring that AI capabilities support the business’s strategic goals.
  • Serve on AI-related planning and policymaking committees, as appropriate, to drive development of technology standards, governance processes, and performance metrics.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field required.
  • Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
  • Minimum seven years of experience required.
  • IT Governance, Risk, Compliance, Security, and/or AI/ML-related experience required.
  • Certification in AI governance, risk, or security preferred.
  • ISACA Advanced in AI Audit (AAIA), AIGP, CRISC, CISA, or CGEIT preferred.
  • Ability to organize and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Accurate data entry skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Strong working knowledge of AI/LLM governance frameworks such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, and emerging AI regulations (e.g., EU AI Act).
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze and manipulate data across various sources including Excel, GRC platforms, and online repositories.
  • Ability to create, improve, and maintain AI governance processes in the IT Division (process modelling and procedure development experience desired).
  • Understanding of systems development lifecycle and change management concepts, and how they apply to AI/ML model development and deployment.
  • Understanding of financial institution governance and regulations including SSAE16/18, FFIEC, NSIT, and ISACA/COBIT, as they relate to AI/LLM technologies.
  • Familiarity with responsible AI concepts, including model risk management, bias and fairness testing, explainability, and data privacy considerations.
  • Ability to stay organized and effectively manage completion of assigned tasks in a fast-moving, evolving technology landscape.
  • Excellent written and oral communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex AI and technical risk concepts for non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to summarize and condense large amount of information and data for executive synopsis.

title: Senior Infrastructure & Cloud Engineer
description:
Hey there!
We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

Behind the user-friendly iOS and Android apps and webpage that work across the world is the engineering team. We are in charge of creating, developing, improving, and maintaining all Fever services so that more people can have an amazing experience.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Infrastructure & Cloud Engineer to join our Infrastructure & Platform team.

In this role, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and operating highly available, scalable, and secure infrastructure solutions across AWS cloud environments and on-premise/bare-metal infrastructure.

You will play a key role in maintaining and evolving our hybrid infrastructure, combining traditional systems administration with modern Cloud and DevOps practices.

Our infrastructure includes dedicated bare-metal servers hosted by external providers such as OVH, alongside AWS cloud services. You will work across both environments, ensuring reliability, security, automation, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on technical role that requires a strong understanding of Linux systems, networking, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, and Infrastructure as Code.

As a senior member of the team, you will contribute to infrastructure architecture, lead technical initiatives, troubleshoot complex production issues, and collaborate closely with DevOps, Platform Engineering, Security, and Software Engineering teams.

This role is ideal for experienced infrastructure professionals who enjoy working across both cloud-native and traditional environments and want to take ownership of critical infrastructure without focusing on physical datacenter operations.

What you'll do

  • Design, deploy, maintain, and optimize infrastructure across AWS and bare-metal environments.
  • Administer and troubleshoot Linux-based servers hosted by external infrastructure providers such as OVH.
  • Manage and optimize AWS services, including EC2, VPC, S3, IAM, RDS, Route 53, ELB/ALB, and EKS.
  • Deploy, manage, and troubleshoot Kubernetes clusters running in both AWS and self-hosted environments.
  • Design and maintain secure networking and connectivity between cloud and bare-metal infrastructure.
  • Implement and maintain Infrastructure as Code using Terraform and/or CloudFormation.
  • Automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, and operational processes using Python, Bash, and Ansible.
  • Build, maintain, and improve CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure and application deployments.
  • Monitor infrastructure performance, availability, and security, identifying opportunities for improvement.
  • Troubleshoot complex production incidents involving servers, networking, containers, and cloud services.
  • Implement and improve backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity strategies.
  • Support infrastructure modernization and future cloud migration initiatives when required.
  • Collaborate with DevOps and Engineering teams to improve deployment processes, scalability, and reliability.
  • Contribute to infrastructure architecture decisions, technical standards, and operational best practices.
  • Maintain clear technical documentation and share knowledge across distributed engineering teams.

About you

You are an experienced Infrastructure or Cloud Engineer with a strong background in Linux systems administration, AWS, Kubernetes, and automation.

You understand how traditional infrastructure works and are equally comfortable working with modern cloud technologies.

You enjoy solving complex infrastructure challenges, troubleshooting production systems, and improving reliability through automation.

You are comfortable taking ownership of infrastructure initiatives, working independently, and collaborating with international engineering teams.

Most importantly, you are a hands-on engineer who understands both the underlying infrastructure and the cloud services running on top of it.

Requirements

Language Requirements

  • English: Full professional proficiency (C1+/C2 or near-native level) – Mandatory.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to participate fluently in complex technical discussions and collaborate with international teams.
  • Spanish: Nice to have, but not mandatory.

Experience

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in Systems Administration, Infrastructure Engineering, DevOps, or related roles.
  • 3+ years of experience working with cloud infrastructure, preferably AWS.
  • Proven experience managing both cloud infrastructure and dedicated physical/bare-metal servers.
  • Hands-on experience deploying, managing, and troubleshooting Kubernetes clusters in production.
  • Experience operating business-critical infrastructure with high availability and reliability requirements.
  • Experience working with international, distributed, and cross-functional engineering teams.

Cloud & AWS (Must Have)

  • Core AWS Services: EC2, VPC, S3, IAM, Route 53, ELB/ALB, and RDS.
  • Networking: VPC networking, routing, security groups, VPNs, and connectivity between cloud and external infrastructure.
  • Container Orchestration: Experience with Amazon EKS and Kubernetes workloads.
  • Infrastructure as Code: Strong hands-on experience with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Understanding of cloud security, monitoring, scalability, and cost optimization.

Bare-Metal & Infrastructure (Must Have)

  • Linux Administration: Strong experience with Linux servers (Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, or similar distributions).
  • Bare-Metal Infrastructure: Experience administering dedicated physical servers hosted by external providers such as OVH, Hetzner, or equivalent.
  • Networking: Solid understanding of TCP/IP, routing, firewalls, VLANs, DNS, DHCP, and load balancing.
  • Virtualization: Experience with VMware, KVM, Proxmox, or similar virtualization technologies.
  • Kubernetes: Hands-on experience managing self-hosted Kubernetes clusters, including cluster operations, networking, storage, and troubleshooting.
  • Storage & Backup: Understanding of persistent storage, NFS, SAN/NAS, backup strategies, and disaster recovery.
  • Security: Experience with Linux hardening, access management, firewalls, and secure infrastructure configuration.

Please note: This position focuses on the remote administration and operation of bare-metal infrastructure. Physical datacenter management, rack installation, and hardware cabling are not part of the role.

DevOps, Automation & Observability (Must Have)

  • Infrastructure Automation: Terraform, Ansible, Bash, and/or Python.
  • Containers: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and container networking.
  • CI/CD: Experience with Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or equivalent tools.
  • Monitoring & Logging: Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, ELK Stack, Datadog, or similar solutions.
  • Version Control: Git and collaborative infrastructure development workflows.
  • Experience investigating production incidents, identifying root causes, and implementing long-term improvements.

Hybrid Infrastructure & Architecture

  • Understanding of architectures combining cloud infrastructure with dedicated bare-metal servers.
  • Experience designing secure and reliable connectivity between different infrastructure environments.
  • Knowledge of high availability, scalability, disaster recovery, and capacity planning.
  • Understanding of workload migration strategies, including lift-and-shift, re-platforming, and modernization.
  • Ability to evaluate infrastructure trade-offs considering performance, reliability, security, and cost.

Soft Skills

  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Hands-on mindset with a high degree of autonomy and ownership.
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex infrastructure problems under pressure.
  • Excellent communication skills when collaborating with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Proactive approach to automation, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
  • Strong documentation and knowledge-sharing practices.
  • Ability to work effectively in an English-speaking, international engineering environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with OVHcloud or other dedicated server hosting providers.
  • AWS certifications such as Solutions Architect, SysOps Administrator, or DevOps Engineer.
  • Kubernetes certifications such as CKA, CKAD, or CKS.
  • Experience with GitOps tools such as ArgoCD or Flux.
  • Experience with AWS Direct Connect, Transit Gateway, or advanced hybrid networking.
  • Experience with WAF solutions such as AWS WAF or Cloudflare.
  • Knowledge of NetApp or other enterprise storage solutions.
  • Experience with multi-cloud environments such as Azure or GCP.
  • Experience participating in infrastructure modernization or cloud migration projects.
  • Familiarity with security and compliance standards such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or GDPR.

Education

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Telecommunications, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Benefits & Perks

  • 40% discount on all Fever events and experiences.
  • Home office friendly anywhere in Spain.
  • Responsibility from day one and professional and personal growth.
  • Great work environment with a young, diverse team of talented people to work with!
  • Health insurance and other benefits such as Flexible remuneration with a 100% tax exemption through Cobee's platform.
  • English Lessons.
  • Gympass Membership.
  • Possibility to receive in advance part of your salary through Payflow.
  • Attractive compensation package consisting of base salary and the potential to earn a significant bonus for top performance.
    • Total Compensation: 65-75k (Including Base and Variable)

About the process

Fever aims to provide the best-fastest possible experience to our candidates. This is how it would look like:

  • Talent Interview - 1h: An intro to Fever, our culture and a conversation about your background and experience.
  • Technical Assignment: Your opportunity to demonstrate all you know! We would like to receive it back within 7 days.
  • Team Interview - 1.5h: A discussion about your proposed solution to the technical challenge. And your opportunity to ask anything you need to know about your day to day at Fever.

Thank you for considering joining Fever. We cannot wait to learn more about you!

If you want to learn more about us: Fever's Blog | |TechCrunch

Fever is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workspace where everyone's background and ideas count. Our main goal is to find the best possible talent regardless of place of birth, racial or ethnic origin, gender, gender identity, religion, opinion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, marital status, age or caring responsibilities. We encourage everyone to apply!

If you require any kind of accommodation during the selection process please contact our Talent team so we can help you by providing a welcoming and seamless journey.

title: Intelligence Research Specialist
description:
Organizational Location: This position is with the Department of Homeland Security, within U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations, National Targeting Center located in Sterling, VA or Washington, DC. This announcement will be open for 5 business days OR until the first 100 applications have been received, whichever happens first. It is recommended that you apply as soon as possible in order to receive consideration.

This position conducts all-source intelligence research, targeting, and analysis in support of counterterrorism, border security, homeland security, and related missions. The incumbent collects, evaluates, integrates, and analyzes information from classified and unclassified sources to identify potential threat actors, associations, travel patterns, movements, and other indicators. The incumbent develops targets; produces analytic assessments, intelligence reporting, and other mission-related products; and coordinates with CBP personnel and mission partners to support targeting and operational decision-making. This position starts at a salary of $121,785.00 (GS-13, Step 1) to $158,322.00 (GS-13, Step 10). Apply for this exciting opportunity to direct programs that strengthen the Department's ability to protect the homeland. Major duties for this position include but are not limited to: Conducting all-source, multi-disciplined research using limited derogatory information, threat indicators, or other leads to identify potential threat actors, associations, travel patterns, and movements, and to develop targets in support of a counterterrorism mission. Leveraging classified and unclassified tools, systems, and datasets to create analytical assessments on known or previously unidentified threat actors, with emphasis on technical signals analysis, network development, and pattern-of-life analysis. Conducting follow-on analysis of selected targets using interview notes, document exploitation, media exploitation, and other available reporting or source material. Drafting, editing, and publishing analytical findings and summaries of action in standardized cable or intelligence reporting formats for dissemination to partners and the broader intelligence community. Establishing and maintaining working relationships with unit personnel and mission partners through training, instruction, and knowledge sharing to facilitate the transfer of intelligence knowledge, techniques, expertise, and best practices in support of CBP's targeting mission.

title: Career Counselor 2
description:
OIC of Washington I Job Description

Position: Career Counselor 2

Division: Education and Career Services

Department: Career Counseling

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities which are required of the employee for this position. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. OIC of Washington is an “at will” employer and employment can be terminated at any time for any reason.


Supervised by: Program Manager

Positions supervised: 0

FLSA classification: Non-Exempt

Minimum Qualifications: BA degree in Social Services or related field. Or four (4) years of experience in supervisory or leadership role. Or four (4) years of experience in budget development and management. Or additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of education

Job Location: Yakima

Salary Range: $23.85 - $31.11 DOE


Position Overview:

The Career Counselor will assist the Program Director in achieving programmatic success statewide. Under the supervision of the Program Manager, this position will work to improve the economic and educational status of eligible students. This position will provide assessments, counseling, education, employment preparation, job development, and related services to adults in a positive and compassionate manner. This position will work with the career counseling services department to provide services to reduce barriers. It is expected that this position will establish strong professional relationships with OIC students, businesses, community partners, and employers to meet program goals and objectives.


Essential Duties:

  • Keep the Program Manager apprised of the progress in meeting monthly and annual goals for the program.
  • Complete the career counseling cohort objectives assigned by the Associate Director and report in a timely manner to the Program Manager.
  • Ensure assessment, counseling, education, employment preparation, and job development services are provided to eligible adults.
  • Manage and guide career counseling cohort in a positive and compassionate manner.
  • Complete intake interviews for potential participants in person and via telephone to determine eligibility for program services.
  • Enroll students and adults who meet eligibility requirements and can provide required documentation into appropriate program services, completing intake forms and getting required documentation.
  • Refer ineligible people to other appropriate service providers, maintaining documentation of the referral.
  • Assess skills, aptitudes, interests, short- and long-term education, training, and career goals, conduct testing, and develop an agreed upon Individual Employment Plan (IEP) for enrolled students and adults.
  • Assess barriers and support service needs of all members of the family unit and make referrals to appropriate providers.
  • Provide emergency services and support services to students.
  • Provide follow up on effectiveness and appropriateness of services provided through referral of students’ family members who are not enrolled in OIC programs.
  • Monitor, review, and document the progress of each participant in meeting the objectives of the IEP. Periodically meet on-site with the program participants and training providers to determine training progress, ensure contract compliance, and resolve any problems.
  • Provide students with individual and/or group career and job search counseling, including interviewing techniques, resume preparation, labor market information, job retention skills, and job development/referral services.
  • Learn and apply knowledge of federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and provisions in providing employment and training services to eligible adult students.
  • Contact employers throughout the assigned region to negotiate and secure on-the-job training; work experience; try-out employment, and other core training agreements, and to develop job placement opportunities.
  • Negotiate and secure classroom training partnerships with training institutions, including community colleges, technical colleges, school districts, and other basic and vocational skills training providers throughout the assigned region.
  • Complete relevant training evaluations during and upon completion of the training objective or placement into unsubsidized employment.
  • Perform appropriate follow-up to verify job retention.
  • Develop and maintain comprehensive case files for each participant, to include the IEP, training evaluations, counseling notes, on-site monitoring reports, and all other forms and reports pertaining to the participant.
  • Maintain accurate and complete participant’s files. Work in close cooperation with other Career Counselors and Program Management to provide case/participant management support as needed.
  • Establish a professional relationship with clients, businesses, and employers to meet program goals and objectives.
  • Establish a network of contacts with potential partner agencies and organizations in local communities to meet the needs of the program and clients, ensure services are not duplicated, and develop a list of referral resources.
  • Other duties as assigned.

title: Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About Us: NEWITY is America's source for small business capital. We’re building a continuous loan-monitoring platform that automates covenant tracking, collateral monitoring, financial-statement collection, exception handling, and borrower engagement across SBA and commercial loan portfolios. Achieving our vision requires more than ambition. It demands resilience, collaboration, accountability, professionalism, and a relentless drive to improve. Our culture moves fast, fosters excellence, and rewards those who lean in. It’s not for everyone, but if you’re energized by challenge, motivated by impact, and ready to grow alongside teammates who share your commitment, there’s no better place to build your career.


Job Summary: The Cloud and Infrastructure Engineer is responsible for the design, operation, security, and continuous improvement of the cloud infrastructure supporting NEWITY's applications, databases, and partner integrations — a multi-account AWS environment with a substantial serverless and event-driven footprint, plus a small set of supporting Azure services. This role maintains and hardens those environments, contributes to automation, reliability, scalability, and performance, and enables efficient software delivery through modern DevOps practices.


This is a hybrid role spanning DevOps, Cloud Operations, and Site Reliability Engineering. The same person builds the infrastructure and the pipelines that deploy to it, runs and secures that environment day to day, and owns its reliability — service health, observability, incident response, and reducing the operational toil that comes with all three.


Security is the first responsibility of this role, ahead of scalability and flexibility. As a financial services company, NEWITY holds sensitive borrower and business data, and we expect this engineer to set and hold the standard for how that infrastructure is secured — including when that means pushing back.


This role works directly with Product Engineering day to day but reports to the SVP, Head of Security & Infrastructure. That separation is deliberate: it preserves the independence this role needs to enforce security and infrastructure standards without being subject to feature-delivery pressure

title: Disease Network Specialist, Rare Endocrinology, EU Center
description:
Mavericks Wanted

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on

In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.

Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work.

What You’ll Do

You will report to VP & GM EU Center, and work closely with our Medical Science Liaisons (MSLs), Medical Affairs, Marketing and Patient Advocacy to drive strategic initiatives that support BridgeBio’s mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients with genetic diseases and genetically driven cancers. During 2027 the reporting line will move to the Senior Director, Commercial, EU Center once that role is in place. Your primary purpose will be to improve the diagnosis rates of autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 1 (ADH1), a rare genetic cause of hypoparathyroidism, by building disease awareness and supporting diagnostic pathways across a broad network of endocrinology centers and practices, with a focus on disease education in the 2027 pre-launch phase. After launch, the role is planned to evolve into a Key Account Manager role. You complement our MSLs: they lead deep scientific exchange with expert centers, you bring breadth across hospital endocrinology departments, medical care centers (MVZ) and office-based endocrinologists. This role requires effective collaboration with cross-functional colleagues and external stakeholders to ensure high-quality execution and impact. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in rare disease field engagement in endocrinology with strong communication skills, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, hands-on environment.

Responsibilities

  • Network coverage: Build and maintain a broad network across hospital endocrinology departments, MVZ and selected office-based endocrinologists in your territory
  • Disease awareness: Raise awareness of ADH1 among physicians managing hypoparathyroidism, helping them recognize when a genetic cause should be suspected
  • Diagnostic pathways: Share guideline-aligned diagnostic algorithms and approved disease education materials, and help centers embed them in routine care
  • Testing support: Support HCPs with the logistics of genetic testing, including family testing initiated by the treating physician
  • MSL partnership: Work hand in hand with MSLs on joint account plans, refer scientific questions to them, and provide operational support at centers of excellence
  • Insights and planning: Capture field insights on diagnostic gaps and referral patterns in CRM, and use them for territory planning and regular business reviews
  • Compliance: Operate fully within HWG, the industry codes and company policy, with a disease-focused, non-promotional remit before approval, and prepare the transition to a Key Account Manager role after launch

Where You’ll Work

This is a field-based position in Germany, covering either the North or the South territory, with approximately 60-70% travel anticipated for customer visits, regional meetings and congresses. Candidates should live within their territory, ideally close to a major transport hub.

Who You Are

  • Qualification as Pharmaberater according to § 75 AMG, e.g. a degree in life sciences, pharmacy or medicine, or certified Pharmareferent/in
  • At least 5 years of field experience in pharma or biotech, ideally in rare diseases, endocrinology or nephrology, and in a key account management or disease awareness role
  • Established network among hospital and office-based endocrinologists in Germany
  • Experience with genetic testing, diagnostic pathways or rare disease diagnostic support programs is a strong plus
  • Sound knowledge of HWG and industry codes, with a proven ability to work compliantly in a pre-launch environment
  • Entrepreneurial, self-driven and collaborative, comfortable building a new affiliate and working closely with MSLs and cross-functional teams
  • Fluent German and good English, valid driving license, and willingness to travel 60-70% of the time

Rewarding Those Who Make the Mission Possible

We have high expectations for our team members. We make sure those working hard for patients are rewarded and cared for in return.

  • Market leading compensation
  • Hybrid work model - we value your flexibility in how you work, but encourage time in the office to strengthen our culture, collaboration, and sense of community
  • We provide career development through regular feedback, continuous education and professional development programs
  • We celebrate strong performance with financial rewards, peer-to-peer recognition, and growth opportunities.

As a global company, our comprehensive benefits may vary based on location. We have high expectations for our team members. We make sure those working hard for patients are rewarded and cared for in return.

For BridgeBio Full-Time U.S Based Roles:

Financial & Rewards

  • Market-leading compensation
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
  • Pre-tax commuter benefits (transit and parking)
  • Referral bonus for hired candidates
  • Subsidized lunch and parking on in-office days

Health & Well-Being

  • 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions, plus Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
  • Fertility & family-forming benefits
  • Expanded mental health support (therapy and coaching resources)
  • Hybrid work model with flexibility
  • Flexible, “take-what-you-need” paid time off and company-paid holidays
  • Comprehensive paid medical and parental leave to care for yourself and your family

Skill Development & Career Paths:

  • People are part of our growth and success story - from discovery to active drug trials and FDA pipelines, there are endless opportunities for skill development and internal mobility
  • We provide career pathing through regular feedback, continuous education and professional development programs via LinkedIn Learning, LifeLabs, & BetterUp Coaching
  • We celebrate strong performance with financial rewards, peer-to-peer recognition, and growth opportunities

By applying, you acknowledge that BridgeBio will process your personal information as described in our Global Candidate Privacy Notice. Questions or requests: dataprivacy@bridgebio.com

We are inspired Placemakers who enhance the built environment with a focus on brand and culture.
