title: Senior Partner Engineer
description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.

Roku is changing how the world watches TV

Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

About the team

The Partner Engineering team’s vision is to establish Roku as the preferred platform of choice for our partners (media companies) to distribute and monetize their content globally. The Partner Engineering team’s mission is to be the technical advocate and point of contact for the Partner’s Engineering organization within Roku to help them deliver the best content viewing experience globally for the Roku user community. On a day-to-day basis, we work with engineers from partners organization to help them develop, test, certify, and launch partners direct-to-consumer (DTC) apps in compliance with the Roku platform distribution agreement. We represent partners’ roadmap and technical needs by working cross-functionally with the assigned Partner Engagement Managers, product and engineering teams within Roku.

About the role

Roku's platform is live across the multiple European countries, and our European footprint is growing — through Roku TV licensing partners, through our own streaming hardware, and through the local broadcasters and streaming services that make the platform worth owning in each market.

You will be the senior engineer for our European partners: the person who makes their apps fast, stable and certifiable on Roku, who represents their technical constraints to our platform and OS teams, and who makes each new market launch a technical success rather than a scramble.

You will be the engineer for a portfolio of European partners — public service and commercial broadcasters, subscription streaming services and pay-TV operators — working with the Partner Engineering team in San Jose and with the Partner Engagement Manager in London who owns those partners’ relationships. You will debug crashes, memory and launch-time issues, diagnose partner-reported streaming problems, and give your partners hands-on support through Roku certification.

How you’ll work with the Partner Engagement Manager. The Partner Engagement Manager from Roku owns the partner relationship, the launch plan and timeline, partner priorities, and communication during incidents. You own the technical diagnosis, the integration work, and technical sign-off on certification and launch readiness, working engineer to engineer with the partner’s technical team. When something breaks, the Partner Engagement Manager coordinates the response and keeps the partner informed; you find the root cause and the path to a fix.

Level: Senior individual contributor, with no direct reports.

Reports to: Director, Partner Engineering, based in San Jose.

Location and work arrangement: London, UK, in the office Monday to Thursday, with flexible Fridays. Travel within Europe up to 40% of your time. Regular late-afternoon calls with San Jose, whose working day starts at 4pm UK time.

On-call: For major partner launches and live events, the Partner Engagement Manager is the on-call escalation point and brings this role in for technical diagnosis, which can mean occasional work outside normal hours.

Expected impact: European partners’ apps pass certification and launch without technical surprises. Additionally, you’ll own the stability, performance and engagement metrics for your partners' apps, and keep each at or better than its benchmark: Roku's certification thresholds and the best-performing apps on the platform.

  • Stability: crash rate, unexpected app closures and out-of-memory terminations
  • Performance: launch time, video start time, video start and playback failures, and rebuffering
  • Engagement: streaming hours per subscriber
  • App Certification and public release: time from technical onboarding to launch in each new market
  • Incidents: platform-caused incidents affecting your partners' apps, and time to resolve them

What you'll do

European market expansion

  • Sign off the technical readiness of each new market launch. The Partner Engagement Manager owns the launch plan and timeline; you work with Channel Publishing and Certification to get global and local broadcasters and streaming services onto the platform ahead of a market opening — scoping integrations, running technical onboarding, and clearing the issues that would otherwise surface on launch day. Then write down what “technically ready” meant for that market, so the next launch is faster and cheaper.
  • Represent regional technical requirements inside Roku engineering. European partners hit constraints that do not exist in North America: built-in broadcast TV tuners on Roku TVs, accessibility obligations, rules on how prominently European content is shown, privacy rules for viewing data, and regional differences in content protection and delivery. You will work out what each means technically, and turn it into concrete platform requirements, feature requests and firmware bugs — and follow them to resolution. You don’t need to be an expert in each regulation but should be capable to work cross-functionally with Roku legal, product, engineering to drive these requests to resolution,
  • Help European partners integrate Roku Pay, working with Roku technical teams: you advise partners on their integration, debug it, and test European purchase flows for multi-currency pricing, VAT and invoicing expectations, strong customer authentication (PSD2/SCA) at purchase and re-authentication, and local payment method coverage.
  • Resolve platform issues on Roku TV and operator devices in Europe. When a TV maker’s or operator’s hardware makes partner apps misbehave, you reproduce the problem, measure which devices and apps it affects, and work it to a fix with Roku engineering teams.

Core Partner Engineering

  • Diagnose and resolve partner app defects end to end — BrightScript/SceneGraph and TypeScript crashes, memory pressure, launch-time and playback-start regressions, general performance problems, and Roku Search integration issues. When the cause is in the partner’s app, you agree the fix with their engineers, who change their own code; you prototype or suggest the patch where it helps. When it’s in the Roku platform, you file it with a reproducible case and work the fix with the team that owns it.
  • Debug streaming and playback problems across DASH and HLS, from manifest and DRM issues to playback problems on physical hardware.
  • Drive adoption of AI-assisted app development to lower partners' total cost of building on Roku. Help partners' engineers use AI coding assistants with Roku's developer tools to build, debug and certify apps faster, feed what you learn back into those tools, and measure the savings in time to certify and engineering effort per release.
  • Get partner apps through Roku certification. When an app fails on launch time, memory, crash rate or playback, you find the root cause and agree the fix with the partner’s engineers, rather than relaying the result. Roku’s certification team runs the review; you give the technical sign-off that the app is ready.
  • Own the technical side of partner escalations from first report to resolution, finding the root cause and driving the fix with the firmware, media, platform and channel publishing teams, and keeping the Partner Engagement Manager and the partner’s engineers informed.

What success looks like in your first year

  • By 90 days: you’re the engineer for a portfolio of European partners, can debug and profile their apps on your own, and have taken at least one partner defect from first report to root cause.
  • By 6 months: European partners ask for you by name. You have carried a certification escalation to resolution and turned at least one European constraint into platform work that Roku engineering is delivering.
  • By 12 months: you have signed off the technical readiness of a new market launch or a major Roku TV partnership, your partners’ apps stay within Roku’s thresholds for launch time, memory and crash rate, and the market-readiness playbook you wrote is what the next engineer uses.

What we're looking for

Required

  • 7+ years in software engineering, with meaningful time spent debugging and optimizing applications on constrained or embedded platforms — smart TV, set-top box, mobile or games console.
  • Proven AI-assisted coding experience: regular, hands-on use of AI coding tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode) in real development work, with specific examples of AI tools used in production workflows.
  • Strong practical debugging skill: you are comfortable taking an ambiguous “the app is slow on this TV” report and working it down to a root cause with logs, traces and telemetry.
  • Working knowledge of adaptive streaming — DASH and/or HLS — and the failure modes around manifests, DRM and fMP4 playback.
  • Experience in a partner-, customer- or developer-facing engineering role, with the judgement to know what to share, when to escalate, and how to say no to an external stakeholder without damaging the relationship.
  • Comfort with data: SQL against large telemetry datasets, and a habit of quantifying impact before proposing a fix.
  • Proficiency in at least one of C/C++, Python or JavaScript/TypeScript, and willingness to become fluent in BrightScript.
  • Based in or able to work from our London office Monday to Thursday, with availability to travel within Europe up to 40% of the time.

Strongly preferred

  • Direct experience with European broadcast or streaming: working at or with a public service broadcaster, commercial broadcaster, European subscription streaming service, or pay-TV operator.
  • Familiarity with European platform and regulatory context — DVB and HbbTV broadcast standards, the European Accessibility Act, the Audiovisual Media Services Directive (AVMSD), GDPR as it applies to viewing data, or strong customer authentication (PSD2/SCA) in payment flows.
  • Experience launching a product or platform into a new country or region, with exposure to the technical, regulatory and partner-onboarding work that involves.
  • Professional working proficiency in a second European language — German, French or Spanish are the most immediately useful.
  • Prior work on smart TV platforms, embedded Linux, or media pipelines.
#LI-ST1

What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?

Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

What are some of the benefits?

Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.

Accommodations

Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com.

What should I know about Roku's culture?

Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV.

We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002.

To learn more about Roku, our global footprint, and how we've grown, visit .

title: Principal Engineer – CPU Hardware Telemetry & Silicon Security
description:
About Cyble

Cyble is an AI-native cybersecurity company building the next generation of autonomous cyber defense. Our products combine threat intelligence, endpoint security, exposure management, and AI-powered detection and response to protect enterprises and governments globally.

We are investing in a new frontier of endpoint protection: using processor-level hardware telemetry to detect malicious behavior at the silicon level.

As part of our Cyble Titan EDR initiative, we are building capabilities that leverage modern CPU architectures, hardware performance monitoring, and advanced machine learning to identify ransomware, malware, exploitation, and other sophisticated threats with high accuracy and minimal system overhead.

We are looking for an exceptional engineer to help build the foundation of this technology.

The Role

We are seeking a Principal Engineer specializing in CPU Hardware Telemetry and Low-Level Systems Engineering to design, develop, and optimize telemetry collection capabilities across modern Intel and AMD processors.

You will work at the intersection of CPU microarchitecture, operating systems, security engineering, and machine learning.

Your primary responsibility will be to develop production-grade technologies that reliably extract, normalize, and analyze hardware-level execution signals for real-time threat detection.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on engineering role with the opportunity to influence the architecture of an emerging category of hardware-assisted cybersecurity.

Key Responsibilities

1. CPU Hardware Telemetry Engineering

  • Design and implement high-performance telemetry collection using CPU Performance Monitoring Units (PMUs).
  • Work with hardware performance counters (HPCs), architectural and model-specific events, and low-level processor instrumentation.
  • Develop collection capabilities leveraging:
    • Intel Performance Monitoring Counters (PMCs)
    • Intel Precise Event-Based Sampling (PEBS)
    • Intel Processor Trace (Intel PT)
    • Intel Last Branch Records (LBR)
    • AMD Instruction-Based Sampling (IBS)
    • AMD Performance Monitoring Counters
    • Model-Specific Registers (MSRs)
  • Identify and characterize hardware events relevant to malware execution, ransomware, privilege escalation, exploitation, and other suspicious behaviors.
  • Implement adaptive sampling, counter multiplexing, and efficient collection across CPU generations.

2. Kernel-Level and Systems Engineering

  • Develop low-level telemetry collectors for Windows and Linux operating systems.
  • Implement kernel-mode components, drivers, and privileged user-space services where appropriate.
  • Work with Linux perf_events, eBPF, Windows kernel interfaces, and native operating-system profiling capabilities.
  • Optimize sampling frequency, latency, CPU utilization, memory consumption, and system stability.
  • Ensure telemetry collection operates safely in production without materially affecting endpoint performance.
  • Design robust handling for processor-specific differences, unsupported events, permissions, and firmware configurations.

3. Hardware-Assisted Threat Detection

  • Collaborate with security researchers and machine learning engineers to transform raw hardware telemetry into actionable behavioral signals.
  • Investigate how CPU execution patterns, branch behavior, cache activity, instruction retirement, and memory-access characteristics can help distinguish benign activity from malicious execution.
  • Develop reliable feature-extraction pipelines suitable for real-time detection models.
  • Evaluate signal robustness against workload changes, environmental noise, and adversarial evasion.
  • Help establish measurable detection accuracy, false-positive rates, and performance benchmarks.

4. CPU Architecture and Virtualization

  • Build a deep understanding of AMD and Intel processor microarchitectures and their hardware event models.
  • Evaluate telemetry fidelity across processor generations and operating environments.
  • Investigate differences between bare-metal and virtualized environments, including counter availability, sampling behavior, and measurement distortion.
  • Develop methods for validating and calibrating hardware telemetry across different hardware configurations.
  • Work with engineering and ecosystem partners on hardware compatibility, performance optimization, and deployment readiness.

5. Production Engineering

  • Build scalable, fault-tolerant telemetry collection components suitable for deployment across enterprise endpoints.
  • Develop benchmarking, validation, profiling, and diagnostic tools.
  • Maintain comprehensive testing across different CPUs, operating systems, and workload profiles.
  • Collaborate with Cyble Titan engineering teams to integrate hardware telemetry into endpoint detection and response workflows.
  • Contribute to technical architecture, design reviews, engineering standards, and intellectual property development.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in low-level systems programming, CPU performance engineering, kernel development, processor architecture, or related fields.
  • Deep understanding of x86-64 CPU microarchitecture, preferably across Intel and AMD processors.
  • Strong practical experience working with CPU PMUs, hardware performance counters, or processor profiling systems.
  • Advanced proficiency in C/C++ and experience developing performance-sensitive systems software.
  • Strong understanding of operating-system internals, kernel/user-mode boundaries, interrupts, scheduling, memory management, and concurrency.
  • Practical experience with hardware telemetry, event-based sampling, tracing, or low-level instrumentation.
  • Experience diagnosing hardware counter behavior and performance measurement inaccuracies.
  • Ability to interpret processor documentation, performance event specifications, and microarchitectural reference manuals.
  • Strong debugging, performance optimization, and engineering problem-solving skills.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have personally built hardware telemetry collection systems, rather than only consumed telemetry through existing profiling tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous engineering experience at Intel, AMD, or a company working extensively with processor performance monitoring.
  • Experience developing CPU profiling tools, performance analysis frameworks, or processor observability infrastructure.
  • Knowledge of Intel PEBS, Intel PT, LBR, AMD IBS, and vendor-specific performance events.
  • Experience with Windows kernel drivers, Linux kernel modules, perf_events, eBPF, or ETW.
  • Familiarity with hypervisors, virtual machine execution, and hardware counter virtualization.
  • Experience with Rust, assembly language, or low-level instruction-set programming.
  • Familiarity with processor power states, CPU topology, SMT, and heterogeneous cores.
  • Background in endpoint security, EDR, malware analysis, or behavioral detection.
  • Experience integrating real-time telemetry with machine learning systems.
  • Contributions to operating-system kernels, profiling tools, processor instrumentation, or related open-source projects.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 3-9 months, you will have:

  • Designed and delivered a reliable CPU hardware telemetry collection architecture.
  • Demonstrated collection of relevant processor events across multiple Intel and AMD CPU generations.
  • Established benchmarking and validation methodologies for bare-metal and virtualized environments.
  • Optimized telemetry collection for low CPU and memory overhead.
  • Built integrations that enable hardware-derived signals to support Cyble Titan's threat detection capabilities.
  • Helped establish a technical roadmap for scalable, production-ready silicon-assisted endpoint protection.

Why Join Cyble?

This is an opportunity to work on a technically challenging problem at the intersection of processor architecture, operating systems, AI, and cybersecurity.

You will help develop technologies that extend endpoint security beyond traditional software instrumentation, exploring how signals from the processor itself can provide deeper visibility into malicious execution.

You will work with a team of cybersecurity engineers, security researchers, and AI specialists developing technology intended for large-scale enterprise deployment.

If you have spent your career understanding what happens inside a CPU and want to apply that knowledge to building the next generation of cybersecurity, we would love to hear from you.

title: Staff Product Manager, Manufacturing Software
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build the software-defined shipyard. That means the full technology stack running Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, ArsenalOS (our manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift), the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

This work is anchored by Arsenal-2, our software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base. ArsenalOS is the digital backbone of that yard. It connects fabrication and outfitting to material movement and inspection. Planners get one real-time view of production. We aren't waiting for the yard to open. Development is already underway here in Orange County, California. The team is proving out the manufacturing methods and digital workflows that will scale across the shipyard network.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Staff Product Manager for Manufacturing Software, you will lead product for the entirety of Maritime Digital Production. Rather than owning a single line of effort, you will set product vision and strategy across MDP's domains: the factory data platform, the manufacturing execution applications, the scheduling and optimization engine, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. You will be the senior product voice for the function, balancing investment across these domains, raising the product bar, and guiding the other product managers on the team.

Product Leadership

You set the product bar for the entire function. You mentor and guide other product managers, establish the product practices and standards the team works to, and create clarity across domains so that individual owners can move fast without losing the thread of the broader strategy. You lead through influence rather than authority, earning trust with engineering, operations, and leadership across MDP.

Product Strategy

You can “see around the corner” for the function, crafting the vision, portfolio roadmap, and critical dependencies well beyond the current cycle. You constantly engage with stakeholders and leadership to solicit input and buy-in, proactively communicating goals and managing expectations. You escalate and own the largest tradeoffs and decision points across the portfolio.

Product Prioritization

You work backward from strategy to set clear outcomes across domains in partnership with your engineering, design, and operations leaders. You build the structures that let multiple teams prioritize competing work within rapid development cycles, and you keep the portfolio adaptable as new information arrives.

Problem Discovery and Solution Generation

You become attached to problems, not solutions. You seek out real-world context through onsite user research on the factory floor, direct conversations with technicians and operators, internal expert feedback, existing product data, and industry investigation. You separate what a customer asks for from what a customer actually needs, capture core workflows, and translate them into well-scoped requirements and success hypotheses across the portfolio.

Product Execution

From design to delivery, you fill gaps wherever needed to make well-scoped solutions a reality across the function. You proactively communicate with teams and leadership, approach solutions with humility and creativity to hit milestones, and set a high bar for how products are deployed, adopted, and supported on the floor.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Setting product vision and multi-year strategy across all of Maritime Digital Production, and making the portfolio-level tradeoffs about where the function invests across its domains
  • Owning the cross-domain roadmap and prioritization, resolving competing demands between factory data, manufacturing execution, scheduling and optimization, and AI initiatives
  • Gathering and refining both functional requirements and non-functional requirements such as tool capacity, performance, and reliability, and setting the standard for how requirements are captured and prioritized across the team
  • Communicating across stakeholders and senior leadership, and exercising the judgment to tell whether a stakeholder truly needs what they are asking for or whether the underlying problem is better solved another way
  • Walking the factory floor, talking directly with technicians and operators about how their work is going, and turning what you hear into opportunities to fix and improve the products across the portfolio
  • Navigating the organizational dynamics between Maritime Digital Production and partner platform teams, advocating from the customer point of view when Maritime's needs differ from how a platform team would prefer to build
  • Aligning and collaborating with the Corporate Technology product organization, keeping the Maritime product roadmap in sync with and aware of the broader CorpTech product roadmap so the two organizations move in step on shared platforms, standards, and dependencies

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 12+ years in a software product management role or similar leading role in product development, including experience owning a portfolio or leading product across multiple teams or domains
  • Demonstrated ability to set product vision and strategy at a functional or organizational level and drive it through multiple teams
  • Experience mentoring or guiding other product managers and establishing product practices and standards
  • Domain expertise within hardware-related industries such as manufacturing, supply chain, warehousing, or logistics
  • Demonstrated ability to gather and refine both functional and non-functional requirements (such as capacity, performance, and reliability) and turn them into a prioritized backlog
  • Strong understanding of the interplay between enterprise systems, including ERP, WMS, MES, PLM, and supplier portals
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence engineers, operations stakeholders, and senior leadership, and to judge whether a request reflects a real underlying need
  • Demonstrated success working directly with end users in operational environments, including time spent on a production or factory floor observing workflows firsthand
  • Ability to navigate cross-team and cross-department dynamics, representing the customer point of view and building alignment when priorities differ
  • Experience aligning a product roadmap with a partner or platform organization, keeping priorities in sync across groups that share technology and dependencies
  • Demonstrated success decomposing complex problems into addressable component parts and arranging the correct sequencing across teams
  • Proven ability to “see around corners” by crafting product strategy well beyond the current development cycle
  • Comfort maturing products from MVP to enterprise-grade production at scale
  • Must be able to travel up to 25% of the time
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience building or owning manufacturing execution systems (MES), shop floor control systems, or operational software for factory, warehouse, or field environments
  • Hands-on experience in manufacturing industries with time spent on assembly lines or in production facilities working directly with operators and technicians
  • Experience with UI / UX web design tools (e.g. Figma)
  • Familiarity with frontier AI tooling and AI-assisted software development workflows
  • Experience in hyper-growth startup-like environments, balancing speed, ambiguity, and long-term platform health
  • Background in operations research, industrial engineering, lean manufacturing, or continuous improvement methodologies
  • Experience leading product across multiple domains or lines of effort within a single function or organization

title: Production Intern
description:
Who We Are:

Gram Games is the studio behind popular titles like 1010!, Six!, Merge Dragons!, and Merge Magic!, with more exciting projects in the pipeline. We are proudly part of the Zynga & Take-Two Interactive family. We do things differently here: we work in small self-managing teams, giving you an incredible amount of ownership, autonomy, and impact.

At Gram, everyone is expected to have a razor-sharp focus on creating a tangible impact on their team, their work environment, and on the overall company strategy. If you are motivated by autonomy, constant improvement, collaboration, and a sense of belonging, this is the place for you.

Position Overview:

Love the process of making great games? Do you like to help guide others through the process from concept through to managing live games? We are looking for a Production Intern to join us at Gram Games and partner with our producers on all aspects of production

You will be a driving force within your team, assisting them with planning and execution to achieve the highest quality. You will empower your team to deliver an outstanding game with high quality, on budget, and on time.

Come join us! You’ll find a dynamic and engaging culture while being a key driver in rapidly delivering features to our players.

Duration: 12 Months

What You’ll Do:

  • Planning & Execution: Working with design, product management, feature teams, leadership, and partner teams, you will ensure clarity of the team’s goals, work with stakeholders and the team to set backlog priorities, and foster ownership of these goals within the team.

  • Communication & Leadership: Facilitate and ensure clear communication, written, verbal, and visual, between disciplines, teams, and individuals. This includes transparent progress, status, and risk reporting, as well as quantitative production delivery metrics. You are adept at keeping everyone in sync with plans and any updates as they happen.

  • Release Management: Ensure high-quality releases by working with QA, Development, Design, Art, Product, and other teams to make sure our releases are well-defined, clearly communicated, high-quality, and compliant with all requirements.

  • Process Improvement: Craft the right processes for the team. Work with your team’s senior leadership to iterate on processes through team input and continuous exploration.

What You Bring:

  • Recent graduate (having completed an undergraduate or postgraduate degree within the past 12 months) in Game Development, Game Production, Game Technology, Computer Science, Business, Information Technology, or a related field.

  • Effective at driving order out of uncertainty, with excellent prioritization and decision-making skills.

  • Influential across both in-person and written communication channels.

  • Effective in one-to-one as well as one-to-many communication.

  • Effective team collaborator and meeting facilitator.

  • Experience with development methodologies such as Agile, Scrum, or Kanban.

  • Experience with project status and risk reporting.

  • Basic understanding of planning tools (such as Atlassian Jira, Airtable, Smartsheet, AI tools, etc.).

  • A real passion for games.

  • Ability to work hybrid from the Gram Games London office at least two days a week.

How to Apply?

You can apply with your CV, cover letter, and a portfolio or showcase of your work, such as game jam projects, personal builds, or team case studies. We encourage you to highlight your role in facilitating team collaboration, project organization, and feature planning across both team and solo projects.

Your cover letter should address the following:

  • Why would you like to do an internship with Gram Games?
  • Why have you chosen this specific internship?

Collects appropriate fees at a refuge entrance station following established accountability guidelines for handling government funds, including cash register and credit card reader operation, performing opening and closing shift functions, issuing entrance receipts, passes, and permits in accordance with established guidelines and verifying validity of passes and permits. title: Senior Software Engineer, Agent Runtime & Customer Workflows
description:
At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny.

Senior Software Engineer, Agent Runtime & Customer Workflows
Customer Agent

About the Role

At Klaviyo, we believe the future of software lies not only in tools that help people work more efficiently, but in intelligent systems that can take action, learn from outcomes, and improve customer experiences over time.

Klaviyo serves more than 167,000 customers and processes billions of consumer profiles, messages, interactions, and conversion signals. This creates a unique opportunity to build state-of-the-art AI systems that help businesses create and execute better customer experiences at scale.

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Agent Runtime & Customer Workflows to join the Customer Agent team, Klaviyo’s AI-native conversational platform. You’ll design and build scalable backend systems and AI-powered product experiences that enable agents to reason, retrieve context, use tools, and take reliable action on behalf of customers.

You’ll be expected to independently own meaningful technical problems, make pragmatic engineering tradeoffs, and help evolve the architecture and quality of the systems you work on.

How You Will Make a Difference

  • Design and build reliable, scalable backend systems and APIs that power AI-driven customer experiences.
  • Build and evolve production agentic systems involving tool use, orchestration, context management, retrieval, structured outputs, and multi-step workflows.
  • Solve hard applied AI problems across retrieval and RAG, grounding, model selection, hallucination mitigation, and deciding when deterministic or hybrid approaches are better than LLMs.
  • Develop evaluation strategies using representative datasets, automated and human evaluation, regression testing, qualitative error analysis, and production signals.
  • Improve production reliability through guardrails, fallbacks, retries, observability, monitoring, and thoughtful failure handling.
  • Build asynchronous and distributed processing workflows that support high-volume AI workloads.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation and help diagnose, mitigate, and learn from production incidents.
  • Work directly with external customers and cross-functional partners to understand workflows, identify pain points, and translate feedback into product and technical improvements.
  • Monitor shipped experiences and use customer behavior, quality metrics, and system performance to guide iteration.

Who You Are

  • You have 5-7 years of professional software engineering experience, with a strong foundation in backend systems and distributed applications.
  • You have hands-on experience building and deploying generative AI or agentic AI applications into production for real users.
  • You are proficient in Python and modern backend frameworks such as FastAPI or Django.
  • You have experience with asynchronous processing and distributed task or event systems such as Celery, Kafka, SQS, RabbitMQ, or Redis.
  • You have strong knowledge of databases, data modeling, APIs, and persistence patterns used in production systems.
  • You are comfortable working in cloud-native environments with technologies such as AWS, containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure automation, or CI/CD systems.
  • You can reason clearly about tradeoffs among quality, latency, cost, reliability, and implementation complexity.
  • You are able to operate independently in ambiguous environments, break down loosely defined problems, and make pragmatic decisions about what to build first.
  • You have experience with and genuine interest in working directly with external customers to understand problems and improve products.
  • You care about shipping useful, reliable products and bring curiosity and sound engineering judgment to a rapidly evolving technical space.

Nice to Have

  • Experience training, fine-tuning, distilling, or otherwise adapting machine learning or language models for production use.
  • Experience with reinforcement learning or feedback-driven optimization.
  • Experience building evaluation infrastructure such as LLM-as-judge systems, evaluator calibration frameworks, benchmark suites, or AI quality platforms.
  • Experience operating AI systems at substantial scale, including optimizing inference cost, latency, or throughput.

title: Junior Analyst, Front Office Operations
description:
About Man Group

Man Group is a global alternative investment management firm focused on pursuing outperformance for sophisticated clients via our Systematic, Discretionary and Solutions offerings. About Man AHL

Man AHL is one of the world’s longest running diversified systematic investment managers, trading in over 800 markets globally and offering a range of absolute return and long-only quantitative strategies that invest across traditional and alternative markets.

With over three decades of quantitative investment experience, Man AHL is committed to constant innovation and evolution of research. It applies advanced technology and scientific rigour to every stage of the investment process, from data curation and cleaning through to signal generation, risk management and execution. It views risk management and trading and execution as central to alpha generation, and its strategies are designed to understand risk, take appropriate exposures and, where necessary, dynamically adjust exposure.

Man AHL brings together scientists, academics, technologists and finance practitioners who are driven by curiosity, intellectual honesty and a passion for solving the complex problems presented by financial markets. It works closely with the Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance (OMI), Man Group’s unique collaboration with the University of Oxford, and leverages insights from its field-leading academic research into machine learning and data analytics.

The Team:

The AHL Investment and Data Implementation (IDI) team is organised into small cross-functional teams, spanning Hong Kong, London, Boston and Sofia with responsibilities for the implementation of all AHL new business (Funds, Investment strategies, new asset classes, new markets, etc.), the integrity of the inputs (data) and outputs (model signals) from the systematic models and long-term strategic development of our systematic trading platforms and processes.

IDI collaborate closely with Portfolio Managers, Quantitative Research, Trading, Technology, Risk, and Business Management to ensure smooth trading operations. IDI members are crucial in testing and implementing changes across various research and strategic platform initiatives. The role offers a high level of exposure across AHL and the wider Man Group, continually presenting opportunities to learn and develop, achieve new goals, nurture new relationships, and reach your full potential. Being part of the newly created Sofia team, you'll have the unique chance to shape its direction and growth from the ground up.

The Role:

As a member of the IDI team, you will oversee the daily management of AHL’s front office investment operations, trading systems and models. You will ensure data integrity, implement new business initiatives and research ideas, manage risk parameters and coordinate projects across a wide range of stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Monitor and ensure smooth operation of AHL's systematic trading systems and models swiftly diagnose and resolve time-sensitive issues intraday
  • Manage daily front office operations, including maintaining and cleansing critical data for AHL's systematic trading algorithms and quantitative research teams. This includes trade signals, data feeds and other inputs used by AHL’s strategies
  • Collaborate with peers and technology teams on projects to improve operational efficiency and contribute to trading platform enhancements
  • Leverage technology including Gen AI, Python and SQL to enhance, automate, and streamline core investment and data management processes
  • Design and support the architecture of AHL’s trading environment, including data aggregation, position management and component monitoring

Skills and Attributes:

Required:

  • Ability to simultaneously manage multiple workstreams and competing priorities
  • Dependable judgement under pressure and intellectual honesty
  • Strong verbal and written communication
  • Strong academic record and a degree with mathematical and analytical content.
  • Interest in financial markets
  • Basic knowledge of Python or similar programming languages for data manipulation and analysis
  • Excellent attention to detail and a highly collaborative personality
  • A keen analytic approach to problem-solving, distilling complex problems to enable timely resolution

Preferred:

  • 1+ years relevant work experience in an operations role in the Investment Management/ Hedge Fund or Financial Services industry
  • Experience steering or materially delivering into complex projects
  • Ability to draw conclusions and portray findings by studying and visually representing structured and unstructured data
  • Working understanding of the financial assets traded by AHL, including futures, FX, equities, options & bonds
  • Experience developing Python scripts and SQL queries for data processing, analysis, and automated reporting

Your unique perspective will contribute to our success, joining a workplace where inclusion is fundamental and deeply embedded in our culture and values. Through our external and internal initiatives, partnerships and programmes, you'll find opportunities to grow, develop your talents, and help foster an inclusive environment for all across our firm and industry. title: Senior R&D Reliability/Test Engineer
description:
About Formlabs:

A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

Your Impact:

The Reliability Engineering Team is the company's independent voice on product robustness, ensuring our hardware products are reliable so that Customers spend more time printing and less time troubleshooting. We architect effective testing strategies, engineer advanced electro-mechanical test rigs, and extract valuable, actionable insights from the data.

Are you a versatile and curious engineer who can see the whole system—from the smallest part to the user's workflow? Can you take complex data and turn it into a clear, compelling story? If so, join our small and agile R&D Reliability Engineering Team.

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop, execute, and manage system, subsystem, and component level validation test plans to ensure products meet design and reliability requirements.
  • Perform hands-on and data-driven root cause analysis (RCA) of electromechanical subsystems and field failures, utilizing common problem-solving methodologies and a "physics of failure" approach.
  • Design, build, and implement automated testing equipment for subsystem characterization and reliability/environmental testing.
  • Collaborate with R&D design teams throughout product development to perform risk assessments, manage continuous testing, and contribute to design reviews, influencing product design for reliability from day one.
  • Analyze field failure data to identify trends, prioritize investigations based on business value, and develop clear, actionable corrective action plans (CAPAs).

Our team did the testing to ensure Form 4 would be the most reliable printer Formlabs has ever built:

  • LCD & Light Engine: Developed custom rigs to simulate UV light and heat, continuously monitoring performance over thousands of hours.
  • Mixer Scraper: Tested our proprietary debris detection hardware to protect the LPU from damage.
  • Z-Axis: Conducted millions of cycles of accelerated lifetime testing to ensure consistent motion.
  • Tank Film: Developed custom pneumatic fixtures to ensure that tank tension remained high after tens of thousands of layers.
  • Cartridge & Dispense System: Optimized cartridge geometry to ensure reliable dispensing of all kinds of Formlabs materials.

Watch here to see a breakdown of these systems in action!

About You:

  • Well-versed with complex electromechanical systems and passionate about understanding what it takes to make them work reliably.
  • Have 2+ years of experience with testing a wide range of sensors, actuators, and mechanical components.
  • Have experience developing system test plans and know how to execute them efficiently within fast-paced product development timelines.
  • Can prototype and run your own tests, from experimental setup to hardware and software implementation in Python.
  • Possess strong data analysis skills, capable of distilling complex test results and field data into clear, concise, and compelling insights that drive action.

Bonus Skills:

  • Familiarity with Linux systems and scripting in various languages.
  • Experience with SQL for data analysis.
  • Prior experience with field failure analysis or quality engineering roles is a plus.

Our Perks & Benefits:

  • Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer
  • An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs
  • Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job
  • 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement
  • Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)
  • Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it
  • Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)
  • Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
  • Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso
  • Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons
  • One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities

You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Compensation

Every Formlabs employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. You’ll have the opportunity to share financially in the value we create together, with a shared incentive to build a business that succeeds over the long term. Equity will be a significant portion of your total compensation, and will increase over time in proportion to your impact. The base pay will be determined by your skills, qualifications, experience, location, and expected impact on the organization.

title: Jail and Court Liaison
description:
Jail and Court Liaison


Make a Difference. Connect People to Care. Strengthen Our Community.


Are you passionate about mental health, criminal justice, and helping people access the support they need? Join Wyandot Behavioral Health Network as a Jail and Court Liaison, where you’ll play a vital role in connecting individuals involved in the criminal justice system with mental health services and community resources.

In this collaborative position, you’ll work alongside correctional staff, mental health professionals, courts, and community partners to promote alternatives to incarceration when appropriate, support successful transitions back into the community, and help individuals receive the care they need to move forward.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys building relationships, navigating complex situations, and making a meaningful difference in people's lives.


What You'll Do

  • Connect People to Mental Health Care: Identify individuals who may benefit from outpatient mental health services and coordinate referrals, appointments, and follow-up care.
  • Support Successful Community Transitions: Participate in release planning and help individuals connect with treatment providers and community resources following release from jail.
  • Build Strong Community Partnerships: Collaborate with detention center staff, mental health professionals, treatment teams, courts, and other community agencies to improve coordination of care.
  • Support Court-Ordered Treatment: Attend Probate Court proceedings and assist with court-ordered treatment processes, including Assisted Outpatient Treatment (AOT).
  • Promote Alternatives to Incarceration: Help identify opportunities for eligible individuals to receive appropriate mental health treatment in the community rather than through continued involvement in the criminal justice system.
  • Coordinate Information and Records: Maintain accurate databases, monitor jail bookings and treatment status, and facilitate appropriate information sharing to support continuity of care.
  • Assist with Court and Legal Coordination: Track court proceedings, coordinate support for court attendance and requirements, and communicate with the Care and Treatment Judge, District Attorney's Office, and other partners as needed.
  • Engage Individuals in Services: Work with individuals who may not currently be connected to Wyandot Behavioral Health Network and help them access appropriate treatment and support.
  • Bridge Mental Health and Criminal Justice: Serve as a key connection between municipal courts, corrections, mental health providers, and community services.

title: Employer Engagement Coordinator
description:
OIC of Washington I Job Description

Position: Employer Engagement Coordinator

Division: Education and Career Services

Department: Education and Training Affairs


Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities which are required of the employee for this position. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. OIC of Washington is an “at will” employer and employment can be terminated at any time for any reason.


Supervised by: Education and Career Services Director

Positions supervised: 0

FLSA classification: Non Exempt

Minimum Qualifications: AA degree in Sociology or equivalent work experience in an upper management position, matched on a year for year basis. Or Two years in supervision, training, education, job development, career preparation, case-management or related activities.

Bilingual in Spanish and English (oral/reading/writing).

Job Location: Yakima

Salary Range: $20.57-26.84


Position Overview:

The Employer Engagement Coordinator is responsible for developing and strengthening strategic relationships with employers, industry leaders, workforce organizations, educational institutions, and community partners to expand employment, training, apprenticeship, and work-based learning opportunities for OIC of Washington participants.

This position serves as a key liaison between OIC, the business community, and the public workforce system, identifying industry needs, developing employer pipelines, and supporting career pathways that align with regional and statewide workforce demands. The Coordinator will also support apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship development, facilitate employer participation in workforce training initiatives, and provide coordination, training, and technical assistance to the One-Stop Operator serving North Central and Benton-Franklin counties.

Working collaboratively with OIC programs and workforce partners, the Employer Engagement Coordinator will promote integrated service delivery, strengthen employer participation, and support measurable employment and training outcomes that advance economic mobility for individuals and families throughout the communities OIC serves.


Essential Duties:

Employer Engagement and Business Development

  • Develop, maintain, and strengthen relationships with employers, industry partners, workforce organizations, educational institutions, and community-based organizations.
  • Conduct targeted outreach to local, regional, state, and national businesses to identify employment opportunities, workforce needs, training requirements, and potential partnerships.
  • Build employer pipelines and business partnerships across priority industry sectors, including culinary arts, construction, warehousing and logistics, transportation, healthcare, and other high-demand occupations.
  • Represent OIC of Washington at employer meetings, workforce events, job fairs, industry convenings, and community engagement activities.

Apprenticeship and Work-Based Learning Development

  • Identify, develop, and expand apprenticeship, pre-apprenticeship, internship, on-the-job training, and other work-based learning opportunities with business and industry partners.
  • Work collaboratively with employers and workforce partners to identify occupations suitable for apprenticeship development and career pathway expansion.
  • Assist employers with understanding apprenticeship requirements, workforce incentives, training resources, and available public workforce system supports.
  • Coordinate with state and local workforce partners to support the development, registration, implementation, and sustainability of apprenticeship programs.
  • Monitor employer partnerships and participant work-based learning opportunities to ensure alignment with program requirements and workforce goals.

One-Stop Operator Coordination and Training

  • Coordinate and provide training and technical assistance to the One-Stop Operator serving North Central and Benton-Franklin counties in collaboration with the Washington State Employment Security Division and local workforce development partners.
  • Facilitate communication and coordination among American Job Center partners to promote an integrated workforce service delivery system.
  • Support One-Stop Operator activities designed to improve customer access, partner coordination, employer engagement, referral systems, and workforce outcomes.
  • Develop and deliver training, orientations, presentations, and technical assistance for workforce system partners and stakeholders.
  • Assist in identifying service gaps and opportunities to improve coordination among workforce, education, training, and employer partners.

Industry Sector Engagement

  • Establish and maintain industry-specific employer networks that inform OIC's workforce development and training strategies.
  • Engage employers to identify current and emerging skill requirements, hiring trends, occupational shortages, and opportunities for career advancement.
  • Collaborate with OIC education and career training programs to ensure training offerings reflect employer and industry needs.
  • Facilitate employer participation in curriculum development, career exploration, work-based learning, hiring events, mock interviews, job shadows, guest presentations, and other workforce activities.

Employer Outreach and Recruitment

  • Develop and implement employer outreach strategies designed to expand employment and training opportunities for OIC participants.
  • Conduct presentations, informational meetings, employer visits, virtual outreach, and other engagement activities with businesses.
  • Maintain an active employer database and document employer contacts, referrals, opportunities, commitments, and outcomes.
  • Identify and cultivate new business prospects while maintaining strong relationships with existing employer partners.
  • Coordinate employer participation in recruitment, interviewing, hiring, and placement activities.

Workforce Partnership Development

  • Build collaborative relationships with Workforce Development Boards, Employment Security Division, community and technical colleges, apprenticeship programs, labor and industry organizations, economic development organizations, and other workforce system partners.
  • Participate in regional and statewide workforce initiatives, committees, task forces, and industry sector partnerships.
  • Identify funding, partnership, and collaborative opportunities that expand employment, training, apprenticeship, and career pathway opportunities for OIC participants.

Program Coordination, Data, and Compliance

  • Maintain accurate records of employer contacts, partnerships, apprenticeship opportunities, referrals, placements, and other engagement activities.
  • Track employer engagement and workforce development outcomes and prepare reports for management, funders, workforce partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Ensure employer engagement activities comply with applicable federal, state, local, contractual, and OIC policies and procedures.
  • Provide timely documentation and information necessary for program monitoring, reporting, audits, and continuous quality improvement.

Community and Industry Representation

  • Serve as a professional representative of OIC of Washington in employer, workforce, education, economic development, and community settings.
  • Promote OIC's workforce development, education, career training, apprenticeship, and employment services to businesses and community partners.
  • Identify opportunities to increase OIC's visibility and establish strategic partnerships that support career advancement and economic mobility for individuals and families.

Other Duties

  • This position requires substantial travel to support organizational objectives to participate in staff meetings, professional development, strategic planning, and agency-wide initiatives.
  • Support special projects and emerging workforce initiatives as assigned.
  • Perform other related duties consistent with the position's purpose and the needs of OIC of Washington.

Special Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Be organized, self-motivated, strong written and oral communication skills, and great customer service skills.
  • Strong working knowledge of various software applications such as Microsoft Software
  • Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships in the business and community sectors.
  • Demonstrated ability to utilize sound judgment, work effectively and calmly under pressure, and maintain confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships in the business and community sectors at the local and regional level.
  • Able to maintain a high level of confidentiality.
  • Substantial travel is required.
  • Experience administering U.S. Department of Labor U.S. Department of Education and/or U.S. Department of Health & Human Services programs serving migrant and seasonal farmworker is highly desirable.
  • Able to demonstrate a genuine concern and respect for all cultures and diverse populations.


Work Environment:

The work environment and physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation will be considered to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. Frequently required to stand, walk, sit, talk, hear, reach with hands and arms, use hands and fingers to handle or move objects, tools, or controls. Occasionally drive a vehicle in seasonal weather and road conditions. Will occasionally lift up to 10 pounds. Occasionally required to reach, push/pull, and stop.


Additional Conditions of Employment:

Successfully pass a Criminal History & Background Check and pre-employment drug test. Valid WA State Driver’s License and proof of insurance if requested.

title: Health Technician (Hearing Instrument Specialist)
description:
Duties are performed across Audiology clinical and patient-care areas at Overton Brooks VAMC and associated Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs). The HIS provides both direct and indirect patient care, manages technical and administrative aspects of hearing aid delivery and maintenance, assists audiologists with evaluation and treatment preparation, and supports face-to-face and telehealth encounters.

Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional Primary responsibility is for patient care, supporting diagnostic and treatment procedures, patient charting and patient education, which do not require a full professional audiology education or knowledge and skills represented by audiology licensure. Support functions include both direct patient care and administrative duties. Direct Patient Care (Full Performance Level) Conduct non-diagnostic otoscopy; identify abnormalities; perform cerumen management consistent with audiologist plan of care. Perform pass/fail hearing screenings without interpretation; conduct immittance screening without interpretation. Take ear mold impressions and fit/modify ear molds as needed. Troubleshoot and repair hearing aids; perform listening checks and electroacoustic analyses of devices. Program previously stored settings into hearing aids; activate remote controls; pair hearing aids and accessories via Bluetooth® technology. Provide patient/caregiver instruction and counseling on hearing loss, hearing aids, hearing assistive technology, communication strategies, and realistic expectations. Administrative / Technical Support Complete visual and auditory checks of hearing aids and assistive technology, including accessories and alerting devices. Register, certify, issue, and track prosthetic devices (hearing aids, accessories, assistive devices); manage loaner hearing aid inventory when applicable. Prepare equipment for patient evaluation and Audiology procedures, including daily biologic listening checks of audiometric equipment and calibration checks of real-ear systems. Restore device settings following repair or replacement; coordinate factory returns when indicated. Assist with setup and delivery of face-to-face and telehealth visits; support app downloads and Bluetooth® pairing in clinic. Maintain comprehensive supply/equipment tracking systems, manage RME and consumable stock, and ensure inventory levels support daily operations. Communication and Documentation Receive and route incoming Veteran communications (phone/electronic) to the audiology team and facilitate follow-up per treatment plan. Responsible for ensuring timely and accurate documentation of all interactions in the medical records and that all encounters are correctly documented using electronic medical record and computerized tracking and ordering functions via ROES. Complete documentation for each episode of care per medical center timeliness standards and code procedures as appropriate for audiologist co-signature. Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 0730-1630, (Subject to change based on the needs of the facility). Recruitment/Relocation Incentives (Sign-on Bonus): Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (Relocation Assistance):Not Authorized Pay: Competitive salary and regular salary increases. When setting pay, a higher step rate of the appropriate grade may be determined after consideration of higher or unique qualifications or special needs of the VA (Above Minimum Rate of the Grade). Paid Time Off: 37-50 days of annual paid time offer per year (13-26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Selected applicants may qualify for credit toward annual leave accrual, based on prior [work experience] or military service experience. Parental Leave: After 12 months of employment, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave in connection with the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child. Child Care Subsidy: After 60 days of employment, full time employees with a total family income below $144,000 may be eligible for a childcare subsidy up to 25% of total eligible childcare costs for eligible children up to the monthly maximum of $416.66. Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Functional Statement #: 01082-F, 01083-F Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized

You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job. All applicants tentatively selected for VA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Applicants who refuse to be tested will be denied employment with VA. Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959. Must be proficient in written and spoken English. Subject to background/security investigation. Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued identification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment. Must pass pre-employment physical evaluation. Participation in the seasonal influenza vaccination program is a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP). Complete all application requirements detailed in the "Required Documents" section of this announcement. As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1 or 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

title: Lead Identity & Access Management Specialist
description:
Wrike is the most powerful work management platform. Built for teams and organizations looking to collaborate, create, and exceed every day, Wrike brings everyone and all work into a single place to remove complexity, increase productivity, and free people up to focus on their most purposeful work.
Wrike is our people, not a place. As a distributed team, we own our growth, stay globally connected, and rely on the product we build to deliver impactful work alongside brilliant minds. You'll have real ownership over meaningful work, a global team that has your back, and the flexibility to do your best work your way. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.
Our vision: A world where everyone is free to focus on their most purposeful work, together.

About the Role:

With flexible, distributed-first ways of working, you'll have the support to do your best work, wherever you are. As the Lead Identity & Access Management Specialist you will be the primary architect and team leader driving our cloud application security posture. Your mission is to balance business agility with absolute data protection across our sprawling SaaS ecosystem (including M365, Slack, Salesforce, etc).

In this role, you will bridge the gap between user enablement and risk management by owning Identity and Access Management (IAM), deploying SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) tools to prevent configuration drift, and governing the entire lifecycle of our business applications. Crucially, you will lead, mentor, and scale a high-performing team of IT engineers with a strong security mindset, fostering a collaborative culture rooted in automation and proactive risk reduction.

Your Impact:

  • By building and automating robust Identity pipelines: You will design, configure, and maintain our Identity Providers (IdP) using SAML 2.0, OIDC, and OAuth 2.0. You will leverage SCIM to automate provisioning and ensure immediate, airtight offboarding to prevent orphan accounts.
  • By hardening our SaaS posture against configuration drift: You will deploy and manage SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) tools. You will establish and enforce security baselines (such as CIS benchmarks) across our key tools, catching unauthorized administrative changes in real time.
  • By governing the security of third-party integrations: You will audit, restrict, and manage OAuth permissions granted to third-party add-ons and AI extensions, ensuring our enterprise data remains inside approved boundaries.
  • By mitigating Shadow IT and assessing third-party risk (TPRM): You will analyze CASB, proxy, and endpoint logs to discover unauthorized SaaS usage. You will partner with Procurement to assess the security profiles of new software vendors by auditing SOC 2 reports, ISO certifications, and CAIQ sheets.
  • By championing technical leadership and team growth: You will build, mentor, and guide a dedicated team of IT professionals. By establishing engineering best practices, leading agile workflows, and promoting continuous learning, you will multiply your impact across the entire organization and cultivate the next generation of cloud security talent.

Your Qualifications:

  • Experience: 5+ years of dedicated experience in Cloud Security, IAM Administration, or IT Security Operations, including 1-2 years of experience leading, mentoring, or acting as a technical coordinator for other engineers.
  • Technical Skills:
    • Deep expertise in identity protocols: SAML 2.0, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, and SCIM.
    • Hands-on administration experience with modern IdPs (Okta or Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD).
    • Scripting capabilities in Python, PowerShell, or Bash to automate security workflows and interact with SaaS APIs.
  • Soft Skills: Exceptional collaboration and communication skills to explain complex security practices to non-technical stakeholders, combined with a pragmatic, problem-solving mindset and proven leadership capabilities to unblock and motivate team members.

Standout Qualities:

  • You hold an industry-recognized Cloud Security certification like CCSP or CCSK (Cloud Security Alliance).
  • You hold a specialized identity certification like Microsoft SC-300 or an Okta Certified Professional/Administrator credential.
  • You have direct experience deploying and running enterprise-grade SSPM or DSPM solutions (e.g., Wiz, AppOmni, Reco, or Defender for Cloud Apps).
  • Leadership Excellence: You have a proven track record of designing technical roadmaps, translating business objectives into actionable engineering sprints, and successfully leading a small-to-midsize IT or Security team through complex migrations or infrastructure overhauls.

Team Dynamics:

  • Reporting: You will report directly to IT Ops Lead, joining a team that values proactive protection and automated operations.
  • The Neighborhood: You will collaborate daily with IT Operations, HR Ops (for automated onboarding/offboarding workflows), Security, Procurement (for vendor assessments), and departmental leads across the company.
  • Our Work Style: We operate in a highly flexible, remote-friendly, and data-driven environment. We live in Wrike for project management, utilize Okta / Entra ID, and scripting (Python, PowerShell) for API-driven automation.
  • Our Philosophy: We follow a Zero Trust security approach. We believe in securing through smart automation and user education rather than simply "blocking" productivity tools.

Benefits & Perks:

  • 5 Weeks of paid vacation
  • Sick Leave Compensation
    • 5 Paid Uncertified Sick Days
    • 2 weeks fully paid w/ medical certificate, additional
    • 4 weeks paid at 80% salary rate
  • Parental Leave (fully paid): 18 Weeks Maternity / 4 Week Paternity
  • 2 Volunteer Days
  • Meal Vouchers (CZK 220 per working day)
  • Annual Prague Travel Card (Lítačka)
  • Hybrid Working Model
  • Benefit budget with flexible options, including a MultiSport card, Canadian Medical membership, contributions to a pension savings plan and additional choices available through Benefit Plus

Your recruitment buddy will be Alexandra Vorobyova, Lead Recruiter.

#LI-AV1

Who Is Wrike and Our Culture

We’re a team of innovators and creators who solve the complex work problems of today and tomorrow.
Hybrid work mode

Wrike is our people, not a place. With 1,000+ employees collaborating across nearly every time zone, we support talent through 10 global hubs — Australia, Costa Rica, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, France, India, Ireland, Japan, and the United States — offering flexible ways of working that include remote work, hybrid environments, and co-working spaces across many locations.
While flexibility looks different across teams and regions, employees located near certain hubs — particularly in Prague (CZ), Nicosia (CY), Bangalore (IN), and Rennes (FR) — are generally expected to collaborate in person around 2–3 days per week, balancing the flexibility of distributed work with opportunities for in-person collaboration and connection.

Our persona

💡 Smart: We love what we do, and we’re great at it because this is our domain. Our combined knowledge in this space is unmatched.
💚 Dedicated: We get up every day focused on helping our customers win. We’re committed to helping our teammates win, too!
🤗 Approachable: We're friendly, easy to get along with, considerate, and helpful.
